TagFilters.N.Key.description_en:
Tag keys are used to precisely search for auto scaling resources
- Tag key length: 1–128 characters
- Parameter - N: indicates the tag key sequence number. Range: 1–50
- Separate multiple tag keys with &
`TagFilters` is used to precisely search for auto scaling resources bound to specified tags and consists of a key-value pair
- If only this parameter is specified, all resources associated with the tag key are returned
- If multiple tag keys are specified, only resources matching all tag keys are returned

TagFilters.N.Value.description_en:
Tag value used for precise search of elastic scaling resources
- Tag value can be an empty string, or if not empty, its length must be between 1 and 128 characters
- Parameter N indicates the sequence number of the tag value; valid range: 1–50
- Separate multiple tag values with &
> When specifying this parameter, you must also specify TagFilters.N.Key

LifecycleCommand.CommandId.description_en:
Cloud Assistant command ID. Indicates that the Cloud Assistant command will be executed on the instance after the lifecycle hook is triggered.
- If the command executes successfully, the policy applied after suspension ends will follow CONTINUE.
- If the command fails, times out, or the lifecycle hook times out, the policy applied after suspension ends will follow the configuration of the `LifecycleHookPolicy` parameter.
 tip
Before associating Cloud Assistant, create the required maintenance command and make sure the relevant instances have the Cloud Assistant client installed. For details, see [Cloud Assistant Hook Association Feature Overview](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/Overview-of-lifecycle-hooks#%E7%9B%B8%E5%85%B3%E5%8A%9F%E8%83%BD).

LifecycleCommand.Parameters.description_en:
Parameters and parameter values in cloud assistant commands
You can set 0 to 60 parameters. Note the following:
- Parameter names cannot be empty strings and can have up to 64 characters
- Parameter values can be empty strings
- The combined length of parameters and the original command, after Base64 encoding, must not exceed 16KB
- The set of parameter names must be a subset of those defined when creating the command. For parameters not provided, the default value will be used

LifecycleHookId.description_en: Lifecycle hook ID. You can call the [DescribeLifecycleHooks](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/DescribeLifecycleHooks) API to query the lifecycle hook ID.

LifecycleHookPolicy.description_en:
Strategy to be executed after an instance exits the suspended state. Possible values:
- CONTINUE: Continue execution
- REJECT: Abort subsequent operations
- ROLLBACK: For scale-in activities, ECS instance release is denied and the operation is rolled back; for scale-out activities, this has the same effect as REJECT
 tip
For a detailed description of the instance change process after execution, please refer to [Execution Process and Strategy](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/Overview-of-lifecycle-hooks#%E6%89%A7%E8%A1%8C%E6%B5%81%E7%A8%8B%E5%92%8C%E7%AD%96%E7%95%A5).

LifecycleHookTimeout.description_en: Duration for which the ECS instance remains suspended. When the timeout is reached, the instance automatically exits the suspended state and scaling out or scaling in actions continue according to the execution policy. Please evaluate the processing time of your custom operations and set an appropriate timeout. Range: 30–21600 seconds (up to 6 hours), must be an integer.

LifecycleHookType.description_en:
Type of scaling activity. When a specified type of scaling activity occurs, the lifecycle hook is triggered and the ECS instance is suspended. Options:
- SCALE_IN: Elastic scale-in activity
- SCALE_OUT: Elastic scale-out activity

EventTypes.N.description_en:
Event notification types
- Parameter - N: Indicates the serial number of the event notification type, values range from 1 to 10
- Use & to separate multiple event notification types
- Values:
	- ScaleOutSuccess: Scale-out scaling activity succeeded
	- ScaleInSuccess: Scale-in scaling activity succeeded
	- ScaleOutError: Scale-out scaling activity failed
	- ScaleInError: Scale-in scaling activity failed
	- ScaleOutWarn: Scale-out scaling activity partially succeeded
	- ScaleInWarn: Scale-in scaling activity partially succeeded
	- ScaleReject: Scaling activity execution was rejected
	- ScaleOutStart: Scale-out scaling activity started
	- ScaleInStart: Scale-in scaling activity started
	- ScheduleTaskExpiring: Periodic rule expiration reminder

ScalingGroupId.description_en: Scaling Group ID. You can call [DescribeScalingGroups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/DescribeScalingGroups) to query the scaling group ID

Eip.Bandwidth.description_en:
Peak bandwidth for public IP, in Mbps. Value range:
- If Eip.BillingType is set to PostPaidByBandwidth, the range is 1 to 500
- If Eip.BillingType is set to PostPaidByTraffic, the range is 1 to 200
 tip
If a public IP is already configured in your scaling configuration and you set this parameter to 0, the public IP configuration will be removed. If no public IP is configured, specifying any of Eip.Bandwidth, Eip.ISP, or Eip.BillingType will add a public IP configuration to the scaling configuration. Any unspecified parameters will use their default values.

Eip.BandwidthPackageId.description_en:
The shared bandwidth package ID is used to add a public IP to a shared bandwidth package. You can call the [DescribeBandwidthPackages](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/bandwidthpackage/DescribeBandwidthPackages) API to query the shared bandwidth package ID. To add a public IP to a shared bandwidth package, the following conditions must be met:
- Both must have the same security protection type
- Both must have the same line type
- The shared bandwidth package must be IPv4 type

Eip.BillingType.description_en:
Public IP billing type options:
- PostPaidByBandwidth: Pay-as-you-go—charged by bandwidth cap
- PostPaidByTraffic: Pay-as-you-go—charged by actual traffic
 tip
To automatically assign a public IP when adding an instance to a scaling group, you must configure at least one of the following: Eip.Bandwidth, Eip.ISP, or Eip.BillingType. If none are configured, no public IP will be assigned.

Eip.ISP.description_en:
Line type options:
- BGP: BGP route
- If your account has applied for static single line, the ISP can also be specified as ChinaMobile (China Mobile), ChinaTelecom (China Telecom), or ChinaUnicom (China Unicom)
 tip
To automatically assign a public IP when an instance joins a scaling group, you must configure at least one of Eip.Bandwidth, Eip.ISP, or Eip.BillingType. If none are set, no public IP will be assigned.

Eip.ReleaseWithInstance.description_en:
Delete public IP with instance
This setting applies only to pay-as-you-go public IPs when deleting instances in the ECS console. For details on public IP retention when deleting instances in scaling groups, see [Instance Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/Managing-instances).
Options:
- true: Delete public IP with instance
- false: Retain public IP after instance deletion

Eip.SecurityProtectionInstanceId.description_en:
Security protection package ID
 tip
This parameter is required when `Eip.SecurityProtectionTypes.N` is not empty

Eip.SecurityProtectionTypes.N.description_en:
Public IP security protection type
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the security protection type; currently, only 1 is supported
- Values:
    - AntiDDoS_Enhanced: Public IP with enhanced protection (can be added to a native DDoS protection instance)
    - Leave blank: Public IP with basic protection

HostName.description_en:
Instance hostname. Valid values:
- Linux instances
  - You can use periods (.) to separate the hostname into segments. Each segment can contain letters, numbers, or hyphens (-)
  - The hostname cannot start or end with a period (.) or hyphen (-), and periods or hyphens cannot appear consecutively
  - Hostnames must be 2 to 63 characters long for Linux systems
- Windows instances
  - You can use letters, numbers, or hyphens (-). The hostname cannot consist entirely of numbers
  - The hostname cannot start or end with a hyphen (-), and hyphens cannot appear consecutively
  - Hostnames must be 2 to 15 characters long for Windows systems
 tip
You can set sequential and unique instance names or hostnames for scaled-out instances. For configuration rules, see [Configure sequential and unique instance names or hostnames](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/Setting-sequential-and-unique-names-or-hostnames-for-instances)

HpcClusterId.description_en: ID of the high-performance computing cluster the instance belongs to. Valid only when `InstanceTypes.N` is specified as "high-performance computing GPU type".

ImageId.description_en: Image ID, the image resource used when the auto scaling group creates instances automatically. You can call [DescribeImages](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeImages) to query the Image ID.

InstanceDescription.description_en:
Instance description value requirements:
- Cannot start with a digit or hyphen
- Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens
- Length must be between 0 and 255

InstanceName.description_en:
Instance name requirements:
- Must start with a letter or Chinese character
- Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), hyphens (-), and periods (.)
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
 tip
You can set ordered and unique instance names or hostnames for each expanded instance. For configuration rules, see [Configure ordered and unique instance names or hostnames](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/Setting-sequential-and-unique-names-or-hostnames-for-instances).

InstanceTypeOverrides.N.InstanceType.description_en:
Specify the instance type for spot instances
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the instance type, ranging from 1 to 10
- Value - InstanceType: Indicates the instance type for spot instances
- Separate multiple instance types with &
 tip
This parameter is only effective when `SpotStrategy` is set to SpotWithPriceLimit

InstanceTypeOverrides.N.PriceLimit.description_en:
Specify the maximum hourly price for spot instance types
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the instance type, ranging from 1 to 10
- Value - PriceLimit: Represents the maximum hourly price for the spot instance type. Value must be greater than 0 and can have up to three decimal places
- Separate multiple prices with &
 tip
This parameter is only effective when `SpotStrategy` is set to SpotWithPriceLimit

InstanceTypes.N.description_en: List of instance compute specifications. You can call [DescribeAvailableResource](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeAvailableResource) to view the available inventory of compute specifications.

Ipv6AddressCount.description_en:
Assign IPv6 address to instance network card
Options:
- 0: Do not assign IPv6 address
- 1: Assign IPv6 address; the system automatically allocates an IPv6 subnet for you

KeyPairName.description_en:
When logging in to an instance using an SSH key pair, enter the key pair name
If you set both `KeyPairName` and `Password`, only `KeyPairName` will take effect

Password.description_en:
When logging in to an instance using the password method, set a root login password:
- Password length must be between 8 and 30 characters
- Password can only contain uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, and must include at least three of these types
- Allowed special characters: `~!@#$%^&*()_-+= |
- Password cannot start with '/' or '$6$'

ProjectName.description_en:
The project to which instances created by the scaling configuration belong. Each resource can belong to only one project
- Only letters, numbers, underscores (_), periods (.), and hyphens (-) are allowed
- Maximum length is 64 characters

ScalingConfigurationId.description_en: Scaling configuration ID: You can call the [DescribeScalingConfigurations](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/DescribeScalingConfigurations) API to query the scaling configuration ID

ScalingConfigurationName.description_en:
Scaling configuration name must be unique within the same scaling group and region
Allowed values:
- Must start with a Chinese character or letter
- Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
- Special characters are not supported for now

SecurityEnhancementStrategy.description_en:
Whether to enable security hardening. Options:
- Active: Enable security hardening; applies only to public images
- InActive: Disable security hardening; applies to all images

SecurityGroupIds.N.description_en:
Security group IDs associated with the instance's primary network interface. You can call the [DescribeSecurityGroups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSecurityGroups) API to query security group IDs. Values:
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the security group associated with the primary network interface. You can bind up to 5 security groups at the same time. Valid values: 1 to 5.
- Parameter - SecurityGroupId: Indicates the ID of the Nth security group associated with the primary network interface.
- Separate multiple security group IDs with &.

SpotStrategy.description_en:
Instance Preemption Policy
Options:
- NoSpot: Create a standard pay-as-you-go instance
- SpotAsPriceGo: System bids automatically; instance price follows current market rates
- SpotWithPriceLimit: Set a maximum bid price for the instance

Tags.description_en:
Tags for instances created by the auto scaling configuration. Tags are passed as key-value pairs, with up to 20 pairs allowed. Key naming rules:
- Key naming rules:
    - Cannot start with any case combination of `volc:` or `sys:`
     tip
    Keys starting with `volc:` or `sys:` are reserved for system use and cannot be created
    
    - Only letters, numbers, spaces, and the following symbols are allowed: "_", ".", ":", "/", "=", "+", "-", "@"
    - Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
    > Tag keys cannot be duplicated within the same auto scaling configuration
- Value naming rules:
    - Only letters, numbers, spaces, and the following symbols are allowed: "_", ".", ":", "/", "=", "+", "-", "@"
    - Can be empty; length must be between 0 and 256 characters

UserData.description_en:
Instance custom data
Custom data must be Base64 encoded and no larger than 16KB before encoding
If left blank, the value is empty by default

Volumes.N.DeleteWithInstance.description_en:
Cloud Disk Release with Instance:
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk sequence number. '1' refers to the system disk; '2' or greater refers to a data disk. Valid values: 1–15
- Parameter - DeleteWithInstance: Specifies whether the cloud disk is released with the instance
    - true: The cloud disk is released with the instance
    - false: The cloud disk is not released with the instance
- Setting this parameter to false does not apply to the system disk. The system disk is always released with the instance and cannot be retained

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceIOPS.description_en:
Use this parameter to configure the IOPS size for the extra performance package of a cloud disk. Only ESSD FlexPL is supported.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk sequence number. '1' refers to the system disk; '2' or greater refers to data disks. Only data disks support the extra performance package. Valid values: 2–16
- Value - ExtraPerformanceIOPS: Specifies the extra performance package IOPS size for the Nth cloud disk:
  - IOPS: 1–50000
  - Balance: 1–50000

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceThroughputMB.description_en:
Use this parameter to configure the extra performance package throughput for cloud disks, measured in MB/s. Only ESSD FlexPL is supported.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk sequence number. '1' refers to the system disk; '2' or greater refers to data disks. Only data disks support extra performance packages. Valid values: 2–16
- Value - ExtraPerformanceThroughputMB: Specifies the extra performance package throughput for the Nth disk:
  - Throughput: 1–650

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceTypeId.description_en:
Use this parameter to purchase additional performance for cloud disks. Only ESSD FlexPL is supported
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk sequence number. '1' refers to the system disk; '2' or greater refers to data disks. Only data disks support additional performance packages. Value range: 2–16
- Value - ExtraPerformanceTypeId specifies the type of additional performance package for the Nth disk:
  - IOPS: IOPS type, use the ExtraPerformanceIOPS parameter
  - Balance: balanced type, use the ExtraPerformanceIOPS parameter
  - Throughput: throughput type, use the ExtraPerformanceThroughputMB parameter

Volumes.N.Size.description_en:
Cloud disk capacity, measured in GiB
- Parameter - N: Indicates the cloud disk number. '1' refers to the system cloud disk; '2' or greater refers to a data cloud disk. Valid values: 1 to 15
- Value - Size: Specifies the capacity of the Nth cloud disk in GiB
    - System cloud disk range: 10 to 500
    - Data cloud disk range: 10 to 8192
- Use '&' to separate multiple cloud disks

Volumes.N.VolumeType.description_en:
Cloud disk types:
- Parameter - N: Indicates the serial number of the cloud disk. '1' represents the system disk; '2' or greater represents a data disk. Value range: 1 to 15.
- Parameter - VolumeType: Specifies the type of the Nth cloud disk. Possible values:
    - PTSSD: Performance SSD.
    - ESSD_PL0: Ultra-fast SSD PL0.
- Separate multiple cloud disks with '&'.

ZoneId.description_en: Scaling configuration availability zone ID

ActiveScalingConfigurationId.description_en: ID of the scaling configuration bound to the scaling group. You can call the [DescribeScalingConfigurations](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/DescribeScalingConfigurations) API to query the scaling configuration ID.

DefaultCooldown.description_en:
Cooldown period after a scaling activity (adding or removing ECS instances) completes
During the cooldown period, the scaling group does not perform other scaling activities. Only scaling activities triggered by Cloud Monitor alarms and scaling rules take effect
Valid range: 5 to 86400 seconds

DesireInstanceNumber.description_en:
Number of expected instances running in the scaling group. For more information, see [Expected Instance Count](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/Desire-instance-number-capacity)
- After you modify the expected instance count, a health check is triggered immediately and the number of instances in the group will change accordingly
- Value must be no less than the minimum instance count (MinInstanceNumber) and no greater than the maximum instance count (MaxInstanceNumber)

HealthCheckType.description_en:
Health check type for the scaling group. Available options:
- NONE (default): No health status checks for instances
- ECS: Perform health status checks on ECS instances in the scaling group

InstanceTerminatePolicy.description_en:
Instance removal policy options:
- OldestInstance: Remove the earliest instance added to the scaling group (**includes both automatically created and manually added instances**)
- NewestInstance: Remove the latest instance added to the scaling group (**includes both automatically created and manually added instances**)
- OldestScalingConfigurationWithOldestInstance (default): Remove the earliest instance **automatically created** by the scaling group in the oldest scaling configuration bound to the group
- OldestScalingConfigurationWithNewestInstance: Remove the latest instance **automatically created** by the scaling group in the oldest scaling configuration bound to the group

InstancesDistribution.CompensateWithOnDe.description_en:
Allow pay-as-you-go instances to supplement preemptible capacity. When there are not enough preemptible instances due to price or inventory, allow pay-as-you-go instances to supplement preemptible capacity. Options:
- true: Allow
- false: Do not allow

InstancesDistribution.OnDemandBaseCapaci.description_en:
Minimum number of pay-as-you-go instances in the auto scaling group. Range: 0–2000. If the number of pay-as-you-go instances in the group falls below this value, pay-as-you-go instances will be created first.
 tip
This parameter only takes effect when the billing type of the [scaling configuration source](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/Overview-of-scaling-configuration-sources) bound to the auto scaling group is preemptible. It does not affect the final number of instances, which is still limited by the maximum, minimum, and desired instance counts.

InstancesDistribution.OnDemandPercentage.description_en:
Proportion of pay-as-you-go instances among excess instances after meeting the minimum pay-as-you-go instance requirement; value range: 0–100
Proportion of pay-as-you-go instances among excess instances after meeting the minimum pay-as-you-go instance requirement; value range: 0–100
 tip
This parameter is effective only when the billing type of the [scaling configuration source](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/Overview-of-scaling-configuration-sources) bound to the scaling group is preemptible.

InstancesDistribution.SpotInstanceRemedy.description_en:
Allow preemptible instance replacement at expiration. When enabled, the scaling group will proactively create a new preemptible instance to replace the current one about 5 minutes before it is reclaimed. Options:
- true: Allow
- false: Do not allow

LaunchTemplateId.description_en: Instance launch template ID. When configured, the launch template is used as the source for scaling configuration

LaunchTemplateOverrides.N.InstanceType.description_en:
Specify instance types
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the instance type, with values from 1 to 10
- Value - InstanceType: Indicates the instance type
- Use & to separate multiple instance types
- After you specify this parameter, it will overwrite the original instance type in the launch template
 tip 
This parameter is only effective when the LaunchTemplateId parameter has a value

LaunchTemplateOverrides.N.PriceLimit.description_en:
Specify the maximum hourly price for spot instance types
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the instance type, with values from 1 to 10
- Value - PriceLimit: Specifies the maximum hourly price for the spot instance type. Value must be greater than 0 and can have up to three decimal places
- Separate multiple prices with &
 tip
This parameter is only valid when the `LaunchTemplateId` parameter is set and the launch template's billing mode is spot instance with price limit (SpotWithPriceLimit)

LaunchTemplateVersion.description_en:
Version of the instance launch template. Possible values:
- A specific template version number
- Default: Always use the default template version
- Latest: Always use the latest template version
 tip
This parameter is only valid when the LaunchTemplateId parameter is specified.

MaxInstanceNumber.description_en: Maximum number of instances in the scaling group, default range is 0 to 100

MinInstanceNumber.description_en: Minimum number of instances in the scaling group; default value: 0 to 100

MultiAZPolicy.description_en:
Scaling policies for multi-subnet scaling groups. Options:
- PRIORITY: Priority policy
- BALANCE: Balanced distribution policy

For details on how instances scale under each policy, see the 'Scaling' parameter description in [Create Scaling Group](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/Creating-a-scaling-group).

ScalingGroupId.description_en: Scaling group ID. You can call the [DescribeScalingGroups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/DescribeScalingGroups) API to query the scaling group ID.

ScalingGroupName.description_en:
Scaling group name must be unique within the same region. Naming rules:
- Must start with a Chinese character or letter
- Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
- Special characters are not supported for now

SubnetIds.N.description_en: List of subnet IDs for the primary network interface of instances in the auto scaling group. The subnet IDs before and after modification must belong to the same private network. You can use the [DescribeSubnets](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSubnets) API to query subnet IDs and their associated VPC information. Parameter - N: Indicates the subnet sequence number and supports multiple selections. All selected subnets must belong to the same VPC, and only one subnet can be selected per availability zone.

AdjustmentType.description_en:
Scaling actions for scaling rules apply to both simple and step rules. Options:
- QuantityChangeInCapacity: Increase or decrease a specified number of instances
- PercentChangeInCapacity: Increase or decrease a specified percentage of instances
- TotalCapacity: Adjust the number of instances in the current scaling group to a specified number

AdjustmentValue.description_en:
Adjustment value for scaling actions, applicable to simple and step rules. Valid values:
- When AdjustmentType is QuantityChangeInCapacity: -100 to 100 (cannot be 0), unit: instances.
- When AdjustmentType is PercentChangeInCapacity: -100 to 10000 (cannot be 0), unit: %.
- When AdjustmentType is TotalCapacity: default is 0 to 100, unit: instances.
 tip
You are not allowed to adjust more than 300 instances per API call.

AlarmPolicy.Condition.ComparisonOperator.description_en:
Rule expression object for single-metric alarms

- >: greater than
- <: less than
- =: equal to

 tip
Valid only when `ScalingPolicyType` is set to Alarm. You must configure the related parameters of either `AlarmPolicy.Condition.x` or `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x`. If both are set, only `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x` takes effect.

AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricName.description_en:
Monitoring metric names for single-metric alarms. Possible values:

- CpuTotal_Max: Maximum in-band CPU utilization. Shows the highest CPU utilization among all instances in the scaling group
- CpuTotal_Min: Minimum in-band CPU utilization
- CpuTotal_Avg: Average in-band CPU utilization
- MemoryUsedUtilization_Max: Maximum in-band memory utilization
- MemoryUsedUtilization_Min: Minimum in-band memory utilization
- MemoryUsedUtilization_Avg: Average in-band memory utilization
- Instance_CpuBusy_Max: Maximum out-of-band CPU utilization
- Instance_CpuBusy_Min: Minimum out-of-band CPU utilization
- Instance_CpuBusy_Avg: Average out-of-band CPU utilization
- Instance_NetTxBits_Avg: Average out-of-band network egress rate
- Instance_NetRxBits_Avg: Average out-of-band network ingress rate
- Instance_NetTxPackets_Avg: Average out-of-band network packet send rate
- Instance_NetRxPackets_Avg: Average out-of-band network packet receive rate
- SystemDiskReadBytes_Avg: Average in-band system disk read bandwidth
- SystemDiskWriteBytes_Avg: Average in-band system disk write bandwidth
- SystemDiskReadIOPS_Avg: Average in-band system disk read IOPS
- SystemDiskWriteIOPS_Avg: Average in-band system disk write IOPS
- NetTcpConnection_Avg: Average in-band TCP connection count

 tip
This is only valid when `ScalingPolicyType` is set to Alarm. You must configure the relevant `AlarmPolicy.Condition.x` or `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x` parameters. If both are configured, only `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x` takes effect.

AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricUnit.description_en:
Unit for monitoring metric threshold in single-metric alarms. Options:

- If the AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricName parameter is set to CPU or memory usage: Percent
- If the AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricName parameter is set to system disk read/write bandwidth: Bytes/Second (IEC)
- If the AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricName parameter is set to system disk read/write IOPS: Count/Second
- If the AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricName parameter is set to TCP connections: Count
- If the AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricName parameter is set to network inbound/outbound rate: Bits/Second (IEC)
- If the AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricName parameter is set to network packet rate: Packet/Second
 tip
Valid only when `ScalingPolicyType` is set to Alarm. You must configure the relevant `AlarmPolicy.Condition.x` or `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x` parameters. If both are configured, only `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x` takes effect.

AlarmPolicy.Condition.Threshold.description_en:
Threshold for the monitoring metric in single-metric alarms:

- If AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricUnit is Percent: 1 to 100
- If AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricUnit is Bytes/Second (IEC): any integer greater than 0
- If AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricUnit is Count/Second: any integer greater than 0
- If AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricUnit is Count: any integer greater than 0
- If AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricUnit is Bits/Second (IEC): any integer greater than 0
- If AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricUnit is Packet/Second: any integer greater than 0
 tip
Valid only when `ScalingPolicyType` is set to Alarm. You must configure the relevant `AlarmPolicy.Condition.x` or `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x` parameters. If both are configured, only `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x` takes effect.

AlarmPolicy.ConditionOperator.description_en:
Criteria for triggering alerts with multiple metrics

- &&: The alert is triggered only when all metrics meet the conditions
- || (default): The alert is triggered when any metric meets the condition

 tip
Effective only when `ScalingPolicyType` is set to Alarm and the `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x` parameters are configured

AlarmPolicy.Conditions.N.ComparisonOpera.description_en:
Rule expression object for multi-metric alarms

- >: greater than
- <: less than
- =: equal to

 tip
Only valid when `ScalingPolicyType` is set to Alarm. You must configure either the related parameter(s) `AlarmPolicy.Condition.x` or `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x`. If both are set, only `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x` takes effect.

AlarmPolicy.Conditions.N.MetricName.description_en:
Monitoring metric names for multi-metric alarms

- Values:
    - CpuTotal_Max: Maximum in-band CPU usage
    - CpuTotal_Min: Minimum in-band CPU usage
    - CpuTotal_Avg: Average in-band CPU usage
    - Instance_NetTxBits_Avg: Average out-of-band network outbound rate
    - Instance_NetRxBits_Avg: Average out-of-band network inbound rate
    - Instance_NetTxPackets_Avg: Average out-of-band network outbound packet rate
    - Instance_NetRxPackets_Avg: Average out-of-band network inbound packet rate
    - MemoryUsedUtilization_Max: Maximum in-band memory usage
    - MemoryUsedUtilization_Min: Minimum in-band memory usage
    - MemoryUsedUtilization_Avg: Average in-band memory usage
    - Instance_CpuBusy_Max: Maximum out-of-band CPU utilization
    - Instance_CpuBusy_Min: Minimum out-of-band CPU utilization
    - Instance_CpuBusy_Avg: Average out-of-band CPU utilization
    - SystemDiskReadBytes_Avg: Average in-band system disk read bandwidth
    - SystemDiskWriteBytes_Avg: Average in-band system disk write bandwidth
    - SystemDiskReadIOPS_Avg: Average in-band system disk read IOPS
    - SystemDiskWriteIOPS_Avg: Average in-band system disk write IOPS
    - NetTcpConnection_Avg: Average in-band TCP connection count

- Parameter - N: Indicates the metric sequence number, values range from 1 to 5

- Use & to separate multiple instance specifications

 tip
Valid only when `ScalingPolicyType` is set to Alarm. You must configure either `AlarmPolicy.Condition.x` or `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x`. If both are configured, only `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x` takes effect.

AlarmPolicy.Conditions.N.MetricUnit.description_en:
Unit for monitoring metric thresholds in multi-metric alarms
- Values:
   - When the AlarmPolicy.Conditions.MetricName parameter is set to CPU/Memory Usage Rate: Percent
   - When the AlarmPolicy.Conditions.MetricName parameter is set to System Disk Read/Write Bandwidth: Bytes/Second (IEC)
   - When the AlarmPolicy.Conditions.MetricName parameter is set to System Disk Read/Write IOPS: Count/Second
   - When the AlarmPolicy.Conditions.MetricName parameter is set to TCP Connections: Count
   - When the AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricName parameter is set to Network Inbound/Outbound Rate: Bits/Second (IEC)
   - When the AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricName parameter is set to Network Packet Rate: Packet/Second
- Parameter - N: Indicates the metric sequence number, values: 1 - 5
- Use & to separate multiple instance specifications

 tip
Valid only when `ScalingPolicyType` is set to Alarm. You must configure the relevant `AlarmPolicy.Condition.x` or `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x` parameters. If both are configured, only `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x` takes effect.

AlarmPolicy.Conditions.N.Threshold.description_en:
Thresholds for monitoring metrics in multi-metric alarms
- Value range:
   - When AlarmPolicy.Conditions.MetricUnit is Percent: 1 to 100
   - When AlarmPolicy.Conditions.MetricUnit is Bytes/Second (IEC): any integer greater than 0
   - When AlarmPolicy.Conditions.MetricUnit is Count/Second: any integer greater than 0
   - When AlarmPolicy.Conditions.MetricUnit is Count: any integer greater than 0
   - When AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricUnit is Bits/Second (IEC): any integer greater than 0
   - When AlarmPolicy.Condition.MetricUnit is Packet/Second: any integer greater than 0
- Parameter - N: indicates the metric index, valid values: 1 to 5
- Use & to separate multiple instance specifications

 tip
Valid only when `ScalingPolicyType` is set to Alarm. You must configure the relevant `AlarmPolicy.Condition.x` or `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x` parameters. If both are configured, only `AlarmPolicy.Conditions.x` takes effect.

AlarmPolicy.Effective.description_en:
Specify the active time period for the alert task.
* Leave blank to make it active at all times.
* To activate during specific times, use a [Cron expression](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/Cron-expressions). This is useful for scenarios like disabling scaling during peak business hours, etc.

AlarmPolicy.EvaluationCount.description_en:
Triggers scaling when the monitoring metric reaches the threshold for several consecutive occurrences. Value range: 1 to 180
 tip
Valid and required only when ScalingPolicyType is set to Alarm

AlarmPolicy.RuleType.description_en:
Alarm task type. Possible values:
- Static: Indicates static monitoring collected by the agent
 tip
Only valid and required when ScalingPolicyType is set to Alarm

Cooldown.description_en:
The cooldown time of the scaling rule ranges from 0 to 86400 seconds.
 tip
If the cooldown time of the scaling rule conflicts with that of the scaling group, the scaling rule cooldown time takes priority.

ScalingPolicyId.description_en: The scaling policy ID. You can call [DescribeScalingPolicies](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/DescribeScalingPolicies) to query the scaling policy ID.

ScheduledPolicy.LaunchTime.description_en:
Indicates the trigger time for the task
- If ScalingPolicyType is set to Scheduled, this is the trigger time for a scheduled task
- If ScalingPolicyType is set to Recurrence:
    - If ScheduledPolicy.RecurrenceType is not specified, the task runs once at the specified date and time
    - If ScheduledPolicy.RecurrenceType is specified, this is the start time for a recurring task
    - Only times within 90 days from the creation or modification date are supported
- If ScalingPolicyType is set to Alarm, this parameter is not valid

ScheduledPolicy.RecurrenceEndTime.description_en:
Specifies the end time for the recurring task. You can only select a date within 365 days from the creation date. Leave blank to keep this task running indefinitely.
 tip
Only effective when ScalingPolicyType is set to Recurrence.

ScheduledPolicy.RecurrenceType.description_en:
Specifies the recurrence pattern for scheduled tasks. Options:
- Daily: Runs once every XX days
- Weekly: Select specific days of the week to run once per day
- Monthly: Select a date range within the month to run once per day
- Cron: Runs according to the specified Cron expression
 tip
Effective only when ScalingPolicyType is set to Recurrence

ScheduledPolicy.RecurrenceValue.description_en:
Specifies the value for recurring scheduled tasks
- If ScheduledPolicy.RecurrenceType is set to Daily, enter a single value from 1 to 31
- If ScheduledPolicy.RecurrenceType is set to Weekly, you can enter multiple values separated by commas (,). Values for Monday to Sunday are: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7
- If ScheduledPolicy.RecurrenceType is set to Monthly, use the format A-B. Both A and B must be between 1 and 31, and B must be greater than or equal to A
- If ScheduledPolicy.RecurrenceType is set to Cron, times are in UTC+8. Supports five-field expressions for minute, hour, day, month, and week. Wildcards supported: comma (,), question mark (?), hyphen (-), asterisk (*), hash (#), slash (/), L, and W
 tip
Valid only when ScalingPolicyType is set to Recurrence

DecreaseDesiredCapacity.description_en:
Whether to modify desired instance count. This option is only available if the selected scaling group has a desired instance count set
- true (default): After deletion, the desired instance count automatically decreases by the number of instances deleted. For example, if the original desired instance count is 5 and you delete 2 instances, the desired instance count changes to 3 after deletion
- false: The desired instance count remains unchanged. After deletion, when the instance count is checked again, the scaling group automatically scales out to reach the desired instance count

ForceDelete.description_en:
When the `DecreaseDesiredCapacity` parameter is set to false and deleting an instance causes the number of instances in the scaling group to fall below the minimum, specify whether to still force delete the instance. Options:
- false (default): Do not force delete
- true: Force delete

InstanceIds.N.description_en:
Instance ID list. You can call [DescribeScalingInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/DescribeScalingInstances) to query instance IDs in the specified scaling group.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the scaling group, with values from 1 to 20.
- Separate multiple instance IDs with &.

LifecycleHook.description_en:
Whether to trigger the scale-in lifecycle hook when deleting an instance from the scaling group
Options:
- true: Trigger
- false (default): Do not trigger

RemoveMode.description_en:
Manual instance deletion mode. Options:
- release (default): The selected instance is released directly
- recycle: The selected instance changes to stopped (no billing)
 tip
This parameter takes effect only when `ScalingMode` is also set to recycle

The specific deletion behavior depends on the instance recycling mode (`ScalingMode`) of the scaling group. You can call the [DescribeScalingGroups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/DescribeScalingGroups) API to check the recycling mode of the scaling group.
- `ScalingMode` is release, `RemoveMode` is release: The instance is released
- `ScalingMode` is release, `RemoveMode` is recycle: The instance is released
- `ScalingMode` is recycle, `RemoveMode` is release: The instance is released
- `ScalingMode` is recycle, `RemoveMode` is recycle: The instance changes to stopped (no billing)

ScalingGroupId.description_en:
Scaling Group ID
You can call [DescribeScalingGroups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/DescribeScalingGroups) to query the scaling group ID.

ClientToken.description_en:
Ensure request idempotency. The client automatically generates a unique parameter value for each request to prevent duplicate operations if the API call times out or encounters a server error and the client retries. Value requirements:

- Only ASCII characters are supported, with a maximum length of 64 characters

Processes.N.description_en:
Process types to restore
- Parameter - N: Indicates the process type number, with values from 1 to 5
- Use & to separate multiple process types. Available values:
    - ScaleIn: Scale-in process
    - ScaleOut: Scale-out process
    - HealthCheck: Health check
    - AlarmNotification: Alarm task
    - ScheduledAction: Scheduled task

ScalingGroupId.description_en:
Scaling Group ID
You can call [DescribeScalingGroups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/DescribeScalingGroups) to query the scaling group ID

InstanceIds.N.description_en:
Instance ID list. You can call [DescribeScalingInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/as/DescribeScalingInstances) to query instance IDs in a specified scaling group
- Parameter - N: Indicates the scaling group number, with values from 1 to 20
- Separate multiple instance IDs with &

ProtectedFromScaleIn.description_en:

AclEntries.N.Description.description_en:
Description for IP entry. Default value is an empty string

Separate multiple IP entries with “&”
Rules:

AclEntries.N.Entry.description_en:
IP entry address range supports only CIDR format

Note:
