Ensure request idempotency. The client automatically generates a unique parameter value for each request to prevent duplicate operations if the API call times out or a server error occurs. 
Value: ASCII characters only, up to 64 characters

InstanceIds.description_en: Instance ID

InstanceIds.N.description_en:
Instance ID: supports up to 100 IDs
- Parameter N: indicates the instance sequence number
- Separate multiple Instance IDs with &

ClientToken.description_en: Ensure request idempotency. The client automatically generates a unique parameter value for each request to prevent duplicate operations if the API times out or the server returns an internal error and the client retries. Value: ASCII characters only, up to 64 characters.

DryRun.description_en:
Whether to perform a dry run for this request. Valid values:
- true: Sends a check request without stopping the Instance. The check verifies required parameters, request format, business limits, and ECS inventory. If the check fails, the corresponding error is returned. If the check passes, the error code DryRunOperation is returned.
- false (default): Sends a normal request. If the check passes, the Instance is stopped directly.

ForceStop.description_en:
Whether to force shutdown. Valid values:
- true: Force shutdown. This is equivalent to a typical power-off operation; all cached data not written to storage devices will be lost.
- false (default): Normal shutdown.
For the following types of Instances, `ForceStop` will always perform a forced shutdown, regardless of whether it is set to `true` or `false`.
- Elastic Bare Metal Instances
- High Performance Computing GPU types: ebmhpcpni2l, ebmhpcpni2, ebmhpchfpni2 Instances
  > ebmhpcpni2l, ebmhpcpni2, and ebmhpchfpni2 are currently in invitation testing. If you want to try them, please contact your account manager to apply.

StoppedMode.description_en:
Shutdown mode. Valid values:
- KeepCharging: Standard shutdown mode. After shutdown, the instance and its associated resources are retained and continue to be billed at the same rate as before shutdown.
- StopCharging: Saving shutdown mode. After shutdown, the instance's compute resources (vCPU, GPU, and memory) are released and billing for them stops. Attached cloud disks, images, and public IPs are retained and continue to be billed.
  For activation requirements of saving shutdown mode, see [Description of Pay-As-You-Go Saving Shutdown Mode](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Economical-mode-for-pay-as-you-go-instances).

Default value: If you have [enabled the default saving shutdown mode](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Economical_mode_for_pay-as-you-go_instances-1#%E5%BC%80%E5%90%AF%E9%BB%98%E8%AE%A4%E8%8A%82%E7%9C%81%E5%81%9C%E6%9C%BA%E6%A8%A1%E5%BC%8F) in the cloud server console and meet the activation requirements, the default value is `StopCharging`. Otherwise, the default value is `KeepCharging`.

ClientToken.description_en:
Ensure request idempotency. The client automatically generates a unique parameter value for each request to prevent duplicate operations if the API call times out or a server error occurs. 
Value: ASCII characters only, up to 64 characters

ForceStop.description_en:
Whether to force shutdown. Values:
- true: Force shutdown. This is equivalent to a typical power-off operation; all cached data not written to storage devices will be lost.
- false (default): Normal shutdown.
For the following types of Instances, the `ForceStop` parameter will trigger a forced shutdown regardless of whether it is set to `true` or `false`:
- Elastic Bare Metal Instance.
- High-performance computing GPU instances: ebmhpcpni2l, ebmhpcpni2, ebmhpchfpni2.
  > ebmhpcpni2l, ebmhpcpni2, and ebmhpchfpni2 are currently in invitation testing. To request a trial, please contact your account manager.

InstanceIds.description_en: Instance ID

InstanceIds.N.description_en:
Supports up to 100 instance IDs
- Parameter N: Indicates the instance number
- Separate multiple instance IDs with &

StoppedMode.description_en:
Shutdown mode. Available values:
- KeepCharging: Standard shutdown mode. After shutdown, the instance and its related resources are retained and continue to be billed at the same rate as before shutdown
- StopCharging: Cost-saving shutdown mode. After shutdown, the instance's compute resources (vCPU, GPU, and memory) are released and billing stops for these resources. Attached cloud disks, images, and public IPs are retained and continue to be billed
  For conditions to enable cost-saving shutdown, see [Pay-As-You-Go Cost-Saving Shutdown Mode Description](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Economical-mode-for-pay-as-you-go-instances)

Default value: If you have [enabled the default cost-saving shutdown mode](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Economical_mode_for_pay-as-you-go_instances-1#%E5%BC%80%E5%90%AF%E9%BB%98%E8%AE%A4%E8%8A%82%E7%9C%81%E5%81%9C%E6%9C%BA%E6%A8%A1%E5%BC%8F) in the ECS console and meet the enabling conditions, the default value is `StopCharging`. Otherwise, the default value is `KeepCharging`.

ResourceIds.N.description_en:
Resource ID

- Parameter - N: Indicates the resource number, valid range: 1–50
- Separate multiple resources with &

ResourceType.description_en:
Resource type, values:
- instance: Instance
- image: Image
- reservedinstance: Reserved Instance Voucher
- scheduledinstance: Elastic Scheduled Instance
- keypair: Key Pair

Tags.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key for user tags added to resources
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag key, range: 1–20

Whether to force shut down the Instance before restarting. Options:
- true: Force shutdown. This is similar to a power-off operation; any cached data not written to storage devices will be lost.
- false (default): Normal shutdown.
For the following types of Instances, `ForceStop` will always perform a forced shutdown, regardless of whether the value is `true` or `false`:
- Elastic bare metal Instances
- High-performance computing GPU types: ebmhpcpni2l, ebmhpcpni2, ebmhpchfpni2 Instances. These Instances are currently in invite-only testing. To request a trial, please contact your account manager.

- PayByBandwidth (default): Pay-as-you-go—charged by bandwidth cap

InstanceChargeType.description_en:
Billing types for Instance and cloud disk. Possible values:
- PostPaid: Pay-as-you-go
- PrePaid: Subscription (annual/monthly)
Please make sure your account supports balance payment or credit payment, otherwise you will receive an InvalidInstanceChargeType error message.

InstanceName.description_en:

- Must start with a letter or Chinese character
- Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores "_", hyphens "-", and periods "."
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
- If the instance has an ordered suffix set by `SuffixIndex`, the instance name length includes the ordered suffix
- When creating instances in batches, you can use the `name_prefix[begin_number,bits]name_suffix` format to customize ordered instance names. For details, see [Batch set ordered instance names or host names](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Batch-configuring-sequential-instance-names-or-hostnames)

InstanceTypeId.description_en:
Instance specifications.
- Instance selection: You can refer to the [Introduction to instance specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Introduction-to-instance-types) or call [DescribeInstanceTypes](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeInstanceTypes) to view performance data for instance specifications. You can also refer to [Instance selection best practices](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Instance-type-selection-best-practice) to learn how to choose instance specifications.
- Inventory query: You can call [DescribeAvailableResource](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeAvailableResource) to check the inventory information of computing resources in the availability zone.

MinCount.description_en:
Specify the minimum number of ECS instances to create; valid range: 1–100.
- The minimum number of instances to create (`MinCount`) must be less than or equal to the creation quantity (`Count`).
- If the inventory quantity is greater than the creation quantity (`Count`), create `Count` instances.
- If the minimum creation quantity (`MinCount`) is less than or equal to the inventory quantity and the inventory quantity is less than or equal to the creation quantity (`Count`), create instances equal to the inventory quantity.
- If the inventory quantity is less than the minimum creation quantity (`MinCount`), creation fails due to insufficient inventory.

NetworkInterfaces.N.PrimaryIpAddress.description_en:
Specify the primary IP address of the network interface card. Currently, only one primary IP address can be specified for either the primary or secondary network interface card.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the serial number of the network interface card. N = 1 indicates the primary network interface card; N ≥ 2 indicates a secondary network interface card.
- Use & to separate multiple network interface cards.

NetworkInterfaces.N.SecurityGroupIds.N.description_en:

- The first N: indicates the index of the network interface card, where N = 1 means the primary network interface card; N ≥ 2 means a secondary network interface card.
- The second N: indicates the index of the security group associated with the network interface card, with values ranging from 1 to 5.
- Separate multiple security group IDs with &.

NetworkInterfaces.N.SubnetId.description_en:

- Parameter - N: Indicates the network interface sequence number. N = 1 refers to the primary network interface; N ≥ 2 refers to auxiliary network interfaces.
- Separate multiple private network subnet IDs with &.

  - Can be empty; length must be between 0 and 256 characters

UserData.description_en:

If left blank, the default is empty.

Volumes.N.Size.description_en:
Cloud disk capacity, measured in GiB. N ranges from 1 to 16; N = 1 indicates a system disk, N ≥ 2 indicates a data disk. Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.

Cloud disk capacity ranges:
- System disk:
  - ESSD_PL0: 20–2048
  - ESSD_FlexPL: 20–2048
    Default value: max{40, the capacity of the image corresponding to ImageId}.
  

- Data disk:
  - ESSD_PL0: 10–32768
  - ESSD_FlexPL: 10–32768
    If this parameter is not specified, the data disk capacity will be set to the snapshot size corresponding to `Volumes.N.SnapshotId`. If `Volumes.N.SnapshotId` is not provided, an error LimitExceeded.DataVolumeSize will be returned.

Volumes.N.VolumeType.description_en:
Cloud disk types and values:
- BV1 (default): BV1
- ESSD_FlexPL: ESSD FlexPL (ultra-fast SSD)
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the cloud disk. Value range: 1–16. N = 1 indicates the system disk; N ≥ 2 indicates a data disk.
- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.

InstanceIds.description_en:
Instance IDs to be tagged

- You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/HBase/DescribeDBInstances) API to query basic information for all HBase instances in the target region, including instance IDs
- You can enter multiple instance IDs at once, separated by commas (,). You can specify up to 20 instance IDs per request, and each instance can have up to 50 tags

Tags.description_en:
An array object containing the tag keys and tag values to be bound
- You can enter multiple sets of tag key-value pairs at once, separated by commas (,)
- You can enter up to 20 sets of tag key-value pairs at a time; each instance can bind up to 50 tags
- Tag keys and values must follow the configuration rules. For details, see [Tag configuration rules](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/HBase/Tag_overview#%E6%A0%87%E7%AD%BE%E8%AE%BE%E7%BD%AE%E8%A7%84%E5%88%99)

AllowListIds.description_en:
The allowlist ID that needs to be bound to the instance.

- You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/HBase/DescribeAllowLists) API to query all allowlist information in a specified region, including allowlist IDs.
- You can enter multiple allowlist IDs at once, separated by commas (,).
- You cannot specify multiple instance IDs and multiple allowlist IDs at the same time. You can only bind multiple instances to the same allowlist at once, or bind a single instance to multiple allowlists at once.

InstanceIds.description_en:
Instance IDs that need to be bound to the whitelist.

- You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/HBase/DescribeDBInstances) API to query basic information for all HBase instances in the target region, including instance IDs.
- You can enter multiple instance IDs at once, separated by English commas (,).
- You cannot enter multiple instance IDs and multiple whitelists in a single operation. You can only bind multiple instances to the same whitelist in one operation, or bind one instance to multiple whitelists in one operation.

AllowList.description_en:
Enter an IP address or a CIDR-formatted IP range.

- Each whitelist can contain up to 300 IP addresses or IP ranges. Duplicate addresses are not allowed. Separate multiple addresses with commas (,).
- Setting `127.0.0.1` blocks access from all addresses.
- Setting CIDR `192.168.1.0/24` allows access from IP addresses within that range.
- Setting `192.168.1.1` allows access only from that IP address.
- Do not set `0.0.0.0/0`.

AllowListDesc.description_en: Whitelist remark cannot exceed 200 characters

AllowListName.description_en:
Whitelist name requirements:

- Do not start with a number or hyphen (-)
- Only Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-) are allowed
- Length must be 1 to 32 characters
- Name must not duplicate an existing whitelist name

- When the resource type is Topic, you can specify 'Read' or 'Write'

When the resource type (ResourceType) is Group, only Read permission is supported; Write permission is not allowed

PatternType.description_en:
Rule Matching Types
- Literal: Exact match. The ACL policy matches resources whose names are exactly the same. In this case, you need to set the resource name.
- Prefixed: Prefix match. The ACL policy matches resources with the specified prefix. In this case, you need to set the resource name prefix.

Resource.description_en:
Resource name or name prefix for the bound Topic or Group
- When the resource name match type (PatternType) is set to exact match (Literal), use this field to specify the resource name. This grants the specified user permission for that resource. You can set this field to "*" to grant permission for all resources of the Topic or Group type
- When the resource name match type (PatternType) is set to prefix match (Prefixed), use this field to specify which resource name prefixes the user has permission for

ResourceType.description_en: Resource type bound to the rule. You can configure "Topic" or "Group".

UserName.description_en: Rules allow access for specified SASL users. You can use '*' to allow access for any user

- Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)

If you do not specify a name when creating the instance, the instance ID will be used as the instance name by default

If you do not set this parameter, the new Kafka instance binds to the default whitelist with IP address 0.0.0.0, allowing all addresses to access the Kafka instance.

Parameters.description_en:
Initial parameter configuration for Kafka instances

Refer to the table below for the list of supported parameters and their default values. For detailed information on each parameter, see the documentation at [Modify Parameter Configuration](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/modifying-instance-parameter).

When calling the API using Postman or similar tools, make sure to escape parameters properly. For example: {"LogRetentionHours":"72","MessageMaxByte":"10","MessageTimestampType":"CreateTime","OffsetRetentionMinutes":"4320"}

Parameter descriptions

- "MessageMaxByte":"10": Maximum message size in MB. Valid range: 1–12. Default: 10
- "LogRetentionHours":"72": Message retention period in hours. Valid range: 0–2160 (up to 90 days). Default: 72
- "OffsetRetentionMinutes":"4320": Offset retention period in minutes. Valid range: 1–10080 (up to 7 days). Default: 4320
- "MessageTimestampType":"LogAppendTime": Message timestamp type. Can be set to LogAppendTime or CreateTime. LogAppendTime indicates the time the message is written to the server; CreateTime indicates the time the producer creates the message

PartitionNumber.description_en:
Partition quantity. The available range depends on the selected compute specification. For details on the supported partition range for each specification, see the documentation at [Product Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/specifications).

Different specifications offer varying free partition quotas. Additional partition fees apply if you exceed the free quota. For the partition quantity range of each specification, refer to Product Specifications. For partition billing details, see [Billing Items](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/billable-items).

ProjectName.description_en: The IAM project for the Kafka instance you are creating. If you do not specify an IAM project, Message Queue for Kafka adds the new instance to the IAM project named `default`.

Region.description_en: Check if the region matches the region in the request when creating an instance; leave this parameter empty to skip the check

SkipCheckVPC.description_en: Skip VPC Check? (For internal service use)

StorageSpace.description_en:
Instance storage space. Unit: GiB; must be set as a multiple of 100.
The available range depends on the selected compute specification. See the documentation [Product Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/specifications) for supported storage ranges and default storage size for each compute specification.

StorageType.description_en:
Cloud disk type for Kafka instance data storage. You can choose ESSD_FlexPL or ESSD_PL0; ESSD_FlexPL is the default. For detailed performance information about different storage types, see [Cloud Disk Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Volume-specifications).
- Use ESSD_FlexPL for specifications with peak traffic over 100 MB/s.
- You cannot change the storage type after the instance is created, so choose carefully.

- Length must be 3 to 64 characters
- Username cannot be admin or monitor, and must be unique within the instance

UserPassword.description_en:
SASL/PLAIN user password. Must meet the following requirements:
- Length: 8–32 characters
- Must include at least three of the following types: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, special characters
- Supported special characters: !@#$%^&*()_+-=

- 2.8.2: Kafka version 2.8.2

- You can use the DescribeVpcs API to query the list of available VPCs and subnets.

ZoneId.description_en:
Availability zone ID of the instance
Kafka Message Queue for Kafka supports cross-AZ deployment. Separate multiple availability zone IDs with commas (,). You can call [DescribeAvailabilityZones](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/DescribeAvailabilityZones-v2) to query the list of availability zones in the current region.

Parameters.description_en:
New Kafka instance parameter configuration

For the list of supported parameters and their default values, see the table below: Parameters Description. You can also view detailed information for each parameter in the documentation [Modify Parameter Configuration](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/modifying-instance-parameter).

When calling the API using Postman or similar tools, make sure to escape parameters, for example: `{"LogRetentionHours":"72","MessageMaxByte":"10","MessageTimestampType":"CreateTime","OffsetRetentionMinutes":"4320"}`.

Parameters Description

- "MessageMaxByte":"10": Maximum message size in MB. Valid values: 1–12. Default is 10
- "LogRetentionHours":"72": Message retention period in hours. Valid values: 0–2160 (up to 90 days). Default is 72
- "OffsetRetentionMinutes":"4320": Offset retention period in minutes. Valid values: 1–10080 (up to 7 days). Default is 4320
- "MessageTimestampType":"LogAppendTime": Message timestamp type. Supports 'LogAppendTime' and 'CreateTime'. LogAppendTime is the time the message is written to the server; CreateTime is the time the Producer creates the message
- "AutoDeleteGroup":"false": Whether to automatically delete the group. Default is false. If set to true, when all consumers in the group are in Empty status and the offset retention period is exceeded, the backend service will automatically delete the consumer group. If set to false, automatic deletion of consumption progress does not affect the group status; groups in Empty status will not be automatically deleted

ClientToken.description_en: Identifier to ensure idempotency for client requests. This identifier is an ASCII string of 1–64 characters, case-sensitive, generated by the client. Make sure the identifier is unique for each request. For details on using the idempotency identifier, see [Request Idempotency](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/Request-Idempotence-v2).

ComputeSpec.description_en:
Compute specification after the instance is changed. To upgrade the compute specification, this parameter is required. For a list of available compute specifications for Message Queue for Kafka instances, see [Product Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/specifications).
Only instance specification upgrades are supported; downgrades are not supported.

NeedRebalance.description_en:
Enable Rebalance
- true (recommended): Kafka message queue will redistribute partitions
- false (default): If rebalance is not enabled, you need to manually add partitions to existing topics to use the upgraded resources
Only select whether to enable rebalance when changing the compute specification of an instance. You do not need to enable rebalance when upgrading storage specification. This parameter only takes effect when the ComputeSpec parameter is specified.

PartitionNumber.description_en:
Partition quantity. This parameter is required if you need to increase the number of partitions.
The value range depends on the current compute specification. For details, see [Product Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/specifications).
- Only increasing the partition quantity is supported.
- Additional partitions added when upgrading the instance specification will incur extra partition fees. For partition billing methods, see [Billing Items](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/billable-items).

RebalanceTime.description_en:
Execution time for automatic rebalancing. Use the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, for example, 2023-01-02 15:04:05. The time must be at least 5 minutes later than the current time.
- This parameter takes effect only when NeedRebalance is set to true. If you do not set this parameter, the rebalancing task runs immediately after configuration is complete.
- We recommend scheduling rebalancing during off-peak hours, such as at night, to minimize the impact of data migration on your business.
- If you do not specify this parameter, rebalancing runs immediately after the upgrade.

StorageSpace.description_en:
Storage space after instance modification. Required if you need to expand storage capacity
Unit: GiB; must be a multiple of 100. The valid range depends on the selected compute specification. For details, see [Product Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/specifications)
Only instance upgrades are supported; downgrades are not allowed

CleanupPolicy.description_en:
Topic message cleanup policies support the following three options:

- ["delete"]: The default message cleanup policy. When disk space is sufficient, messages are retained within the maximum retention period. If disk space is low, older messages are deleted early to ensure service availability.

Note

The default disk cleanup threshold for Kafka instances is 90%. Actual values may vary. For details, see Setting Disk Cleanup Threshold.


- ["compact"]: The COMPACT cleanup policy consolidates messages by key. For messages with the same key, only the latest value is kept; older records are removed.
- ["delete","compact"]: Enables both DELETE and COMPACT cleanup policies. Messages are deleted if they meet the criteria of either policy.

The COMPACT cleanup policy cannot be enabled for messages without a key.

Parameters.description_en:
Kafka topic-level parameter configuration

For the list of supported parameters and their default values, see the table below: Topic Parameters. For detailed information on each parameter, refer to the documentation [Modify Parameter Configuration](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/modifying-instance-parameter).

When calling the API using Postman or similar tools, make sure to escape characters as shown: {\"LogRetentionHours\":\"72\",\"MessageMaxByte\":\"10\",\"MinInsyncReplicaNumber\":\"2\"}.

Parameter descriptions

- "MinInsyncReplicaNumber":"2": Minimum number of in-sync replicas. If the number of in-sync replicas falls below this value, messages cannot be written to the topic. Increasing this value improves data reliability but reduces availability. The default is the number of replicas minus one. For better topic availability, set this to the number of replicas minus one.
- "MessageMaxByte":"10": Maximum message size in MB. Valid range: 1–12. By default, this follows the instance's maximum message size setting.
- "LogRetentionHours":"72": Message retention period in hours. Valid range: 0–2160 (up to 90 days). By default, this follows the instance's message retention period setting.

PartitionNumber.description_en: Number of partitions for this topic. The greater the number of partitions, the higher the consumption concurrency. You can only increase this value; you cannot decrease it. Do not exceed the remaining available partition count in the Kafka instance.

ReplicaNumber.description_en:
The number of replicas for a partition indicates how many copies of the data are backed up. If one broker fails, data remains available. A higher replica count increases reliability.
- Increasing the replica count uses more instance disk capacity; make sure you have enough capacity.
- Adding replicas consumes instance bandwidth resources; we recommend making changes during business off-peak hours.
- Reducing the replica count lowers data availability; proceed with caution.
- Topics with only 1 replica cannot ensure data reliability and are unavailable for read/write operations during instance upgrades; we recommend using 2 or 3 replicas.

    AccountName: Account name for the Redis instance
    AccountPassword: Password for the Redis instance
    If SecretSubType is SingleUser, Accounts must contain 1 item. If SecretSubType is DoubleUsers, Accounts must contain 2 items. AccountName is required, and the two AccountNames must be different.

When SecretType is set to ECS, the SecretValue format is:
    If SecretSubType is Password: {"UserName":"","Password":""}
    UserName: Username for logging in to the ECS instance
    Password: Password for logging in to the ECS instance
    If SecretSubType is SSHKey: {"UserName":"","PublicKey":"","PrivateKey":""}
    PublicKey: SSH public key for logging in to the ECS instance
    PrivateKey: Private key for logging in to the ECS instance

        When Key is KeyUsage: Options are ENCRYPT_DECRYPT, SIGN_VERIFY. Case-sensitive. Example: ["ENCRYPT_DECRYPT","SIGN_VERIFY"]
        When Key is ProtectionLevel: Options are SOFTWARE, HSM. Case-sensitive. Example: ["SOFTWARE","HSM"]
        When Key is RotateState: Options are Enable, Disable. Case-sensitive. Example: ["Enable","Disable"]

TimeRangeStart.description_en:

InstanceIds.description_en:
Instance IDs for tag binding

- You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describedbinstances) API to view basic information for all MongoDB instances in the target region, including instance IDs
- You can enter multiple instance IDs at once, separated by commas (,). You can specify up to 20 instance IDs at a time

Tags.description_en: Array object of tag keys and tag values that need to be bound

AllowListIds.description_en:
Whitelist ID required to bind to the instance

- You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describeallowlists) API to query all whitelists in a specified region, including whitelist IDs
- You can enter multiple whitelist IDs at once, separated by English commas (,)
- You cannot enter multiple instance IDs and whitelist IDs at the same time. You can only bind multiple instances to the same whitelist at once, or bind one instance to multiple whitelists at once

InstanceIds.description_en:
Instance ID(s) required to bind to the whitelist.

- You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describedbinstances) API to query basic information for all MongoDB instances in the target region, including instance IDs.
- You can enter multiple instance IDs at once, separated by commas (,).
- You cannot specify multiple instance IDs and multiple whitelists in a single operation. You can only bind multiple instances to the same whitelist at once, or bind one instance to multiple whitelists at once.

AllowList.description_en:
Enter an IP address or a CIDR-formatted IP range

- Each whitelist group supports up to 1000 IP addresses or CIDR-formatted IP ranges
- Duplicate addresses are not allowed; separate multiple addresses with commas (,)
- Setting `0.0.0.0/0` allows access from all addresses
- Setting `127.0.0.1` blocks access from all addresses
- Setting both `0.0.0.0/0` and `127.0.0.1` allows access from all addresses
- Setting CIDR `192.168.1.0/24` allows access from IP addresses within that subnet
- Setting `192.168.1.1` allows access only from that IP address

AllowListCategory.description_en:
Whitelist type. Available values:

- `Ordinary` (default): Ordinary whitelist
- `Default`: Default whitelist
Each BytePlus account can set up to one default whitelist per region. When you set a new default whitelist, it automatically replaces the previous one, which will become a non-default whitelist. For more details, see [Constraints and limitations](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/product-limit).

AllowListDesc.description_en:
Whitelist remark must not exceed 200 characters.
If this parameter is not set, the remark for a new whitelist will be empty by default.

AllowListName.description_en:
Whitelist name requirements:

- Must not start with a number or hyphen (-)
- May contain only Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters

AllowListType.description_en: Type of IP address in the whitelist. Only `IPv4` addresses are supported

ProjectName.description_en:
Set the project to which the whitelist belongs
A project is a virtual concept that includes a group of resources, users, and roles. Projects let you view and manage resources in a unified way, and control user and role permissions within the project. For more details, see [Resource Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6649/94333).
If you do not set this parameter, the newly created whitelist will be added to the default project.

BackupMode.description_en:
Backup method. Available values:
- `Full`: full backup
- `Increment`: incremental backup

BackupType.description_en:
Backup type. Valid values are as follows:
- `Physical`: Physical backup
- `Logical` (default): Logical backup
Whether you perform a logical backup or a physical backup, the backup target is always data. For more information, see [Backup Methods](../6447/71010#备份方式) and [Backup Targets](../6447/71010#备份对象).

InstanceId.description_en:
Instance ID.
You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](../6447/100741) API to query the basic information of all MongoDB instances in the target region, including the instance ID.

AccountName.description_en: Name of the database account.

AccountPassword.description_en:
Password for the database account.

The password must meet the following requirements:

- Must include at least three of the following: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, or special characters.
- Special characters include `!@#$%^&*()_+-=`.
- Length must be 8–32 characters.

AuthDB.description_en:
Database to which the account belongs

 The default value is "admin"

InstanceId.description_en:
Instance ID.

You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](../6447/100741) API to query basic information for all MongoDB instances in the target region, including the instance ID.

AllShard.description_en:
Whether to batch create connection addresses for all shard partitions in the current instance. Valid values:
- `true`: Batch create
- `false`: Do not batch create
- This parameter applies only to sharded cluster instances.
- When requesting connection addresses for shards or ConfigServer components in a sharded cluster, you are only allowed to select one parameter from `ObjectId`, `ObjectIds`, or `AllShard` to pass in. Otherwise, the API call will return an error.

EipIds.description_en:
List of EIP IDs to bind when applying for a public network address

- This parameter is required only when `NetworkType` is set to `Public`. The number of EIP IDs you need to provide depends on the instance or component type:
  - When applying for a public network address for Mongos nodes, the number of EIP IDs must match the number of `MongosNodeIds`. For example, if you provide only one Mongos node ID, you only need to provide one EIP ID.
  - When applying for a public network address for replica set instances, Shard nodes, or ConfigServer nodes, you must provide two EIP IDs for each instance or component. For details on the number of EIP IDs required for each public network address, see [View connection addresses](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/addresses-introduction).
- You can call the [DescribeEipAddresses](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/eip/DescribeEipAddressAttributes) API to query the list of all EIP information, including available EIP IDs.

InstanceId.description_en:
Instance ID

You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describedbinstances) API to query basic information for all MongoDB instances in the target region, including the instance ID.

MongosNodeIds.description_en:
Mongos node ID(s) for which you want to apply for a public connection address

- This parameter is required only when applying for public connection addresses for Mongos nodes in a sharded cluster instance
- You can apply for public connection addresses for multiple Mongos nodes at the same time; separate multiple Mongos node IDs with commas (,)
- You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describedbinstancedetail) API to query information about all Mongos nodes in the target sharded cluster instance, including their node IDs

NetworkType.description_en:
Network type for connection address. Available options:

- `Private` (default): Private network connection address
- `Public`: Public network connection address

ObjectId.description_en:
Single Shard or ConfigServer component ID for which you need to create a connection address

- This parameter applies only to sharded cluster instances
- When requesting a connection address for a Shard or ConfigServer component in a sharded cluster, you can only select one parameter from `ObjectId`, `ObjectIds`, or `AllShard`. Otherwise, the API call will return an error
- You can use the [DescribeDBEndpoint](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describedbendpoint) API to view all component IDs in the target sharded cluster instance
- Currently, you can only create connection addresses at the instance or component level via the API. Creating a separate connection address for a specific node (such as a primary or secondary node) within a component is not supported

ObjectIds.description_en:
List of Shard or ConfigServer component IDs for which connection addresses need to be created
- This parameter applies only to sharded cluster instances
- When requesting a connection address for a Shard or ConfigServer component in a sharded cluster, you can only pass one of the following parameters: `ObjectId`, `ObjectIds`, or `AllShard`. Otherwise, the API call will fail
- You can use the [DescribeDBEndpoint](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describedbendpoint) API to view all component IDs under the target sharded cluster instance
- Currently, you can only create connection addresses at the instance or component level via the API. Creating separate connection addresses for individual nodes (such as primary or secondary nodes) within a component is not supported

AllowListIds.description_en:
Allowlist ID list. The new instance will be bound to the specified allowlist.
* You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describeallowlists) API to query all IP allowlist information under your account in the specified region, including allowlist ID information.
* Each instance supports binding up to 100 allowlists, and you can batch bind up to 100 allowlists at a time.

AutoRenew.description_en:
Enable auto-renewal. Value options:

* `false` (default): Auto-renewal is disabled.
* `true`: Auto-renewal is enabled.

This parameter is required when `ChargeType` is set to `Prepaid`.

ChargeType.description_en:
Instance billing type. Available options:
- `PostPaid` (default): Pay-as-you-go (also called postpaid)
- `Prepaid`: Yearly/monthly subscription (also called prepaid)

For more information about billing types, see [Billing Types](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/billing-method).

ConfigServerNodeSpec.description_en:
Specification code for the ConfigServer node in a sharded cluster. Default value: `mongo.config.2c4g`.
* This parameter is valid only when the instance type is a sharded cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`).
* You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view the specification information for sharded cluster instances, including specification codes.

ConfigServerStorageSpaceGB.description_en:
Storage space for ConfigServer in a sharded cluster, in GiB. Step size: 10. Default value: 20.
* This parameter is valid only when the instance type is a sharded cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`).
* The maximum supported storage space varies by node specification. You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view MongoDB instance specifications, including storage space specifications supported by different nodes.

Count.description_en:
Number of instances to create. Must be a positive integer greater than or equal to 1. Default is 1.
* Each BytePlus primary account can purchase up to 30 MongoDB instances per region by default. Therefore, when using this API to create instances in bulk, you can create up to 30 instances per request by default. To increase your quota and purchase more instances, go to the **Quota Center** and submit a [quota request](https://console.volcengine.com/quota/productList/coParameterList?ProviderCode=MongoDB_ToB).
* If you specify an instance name and purchase multiple instances at the same time, the system will append a number to the end of each instance name according to the relevant rules for differentiation. For more details, see the rules for **Instance Name** in the [Create Instance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/create-instance#%E6%93%8D%E4%BD%9C%E6%AD%A5%E9%AA%A4) parameter configuration table.

DBEngine.description_en: Database engine. Value is fixed as `MongoDB`.

DBEngineVersion.description_en:
Database engine version. Available options:

- `MongoDB_4_0` (default): MongoDB version 4.0.
- `MongoDB_4_2`: MongoDB version 4.2.
- `MongoDB_4_4`: MongoDB version 4.4.
- `MongoDB_5_0`: MongoDB version 5.0.
- `MongoDB_6_0`: MongoDB version 6.0.
- `MongoDB_7_0`: MongoDB version 7.0.
For more details about MongoDB versions, see [Version introduction](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/version_introduction).

DBInstanceParamTemplateId.description_en:
Select the parameter template ID to apply to the instance.
* Currently, only replica set instances (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ReplicaSet`) support parameter templates, so this parameter only applies to replica set instances. For more details about parameter templates, see [Parameter Template Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/parameter-template-overview).
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceParamTpl](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6447/1362939) API to query all parameter templates under your account and region, including parameter template ID information.
* If this parameter is not specified, no parameter template will be used, and all instance parameters will use default values.
   For example, if you create a new replica set instance with MongoDB version 6.0 and do not specify this parameter, the instance will use the system parameter template for MongoDB 6.0 by default.
* If you select a custom parameter template, but the template does not include all parameters supported by the instance, the instance will use the values from the template for included parameters, and default values for parameters not in the template.

InstanceName.description_en:
Instance name. The name must meet the following requirements:

* Cannot start with a digit or a hyphen (-)
* Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, digits, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)
* Must be 2–64 characters in length

* If this parameter is not specified, the instance ID will be used as the instance name by default
* You can customize the instance name as needed; uniqueness is not required
* If you set an instance name and purchase multiple instances at once, the system will append a number to the end of each instance name according to specific rules for differentiation. For more details, see the rules for **Instance Name** in the parameter configuration table of [Create Instance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/create-instance#%E6%93%8D%E4%BD%9C%E6%AD%A5%E9%AA%A4)

InstanceType.description_en:
MongoDB instance types. Available options:

- `ReplicaSet` (default): Replica set
- `ShardedCluster`: Sharded cluster

MongosNodeNumber.description_en:
Number of Mongos nodes in a sharded cluster. Value range: 2–32.
This parameter is required when the instance type is a sharded cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`).

MongosNodeSpec.description_en:
Specification code for Mongos nodes in the sharded cluster.
* If the instance type is sharded cluster (i.e., `InstanceType` is `ShardedCluster`), this parameter is required.
* You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view the instance specification information for sharded clusters, including specification codes.

NodeAvailabilityZone.description_en:
Add read-only node information, including the availability zone and number of read-only nodes
Leave this parameter blank to avoid adding any read-only nodes to the instance. For more information about read-only nodes, see [MongoDB Read-Only Node](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/managing_read_only_nodes).

NodeNumber.description_en:
Number of nodes:

* If the instance type is replica set (i.e., `InstanceType` is `ReplicaSet`), this parameter specifies the number of compute nodes in the replica set instance.
* If the instance type is sharded cluster (i.e., `InstanceType` is `ShardedCluster`), this parameter specifies the number of nodes in each Shard.

Currently, each replica set instance and each Shard only support 3 nodes. The value is fixed at `3`.

NodeSpec.description_en:
Specification code for the instance. Details:

* If the instance type is replica set (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ReplicaSet`), this parameter specifies the compute node specification for the replica set instance.
* If the instance type is sharded cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`), this parameter specifies the specification for the Shard node.

You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view instance specification information, including specification codes.

Period.description_en:
Purchase duration for subscription instances:

* If `PeriodUnit` is `Year`, `Period` can be 1–3
* If `PeriodUnit` is `Month`, `Period` can be 1–9

When `ChargeType` is set to `Prepaid`, this parameter is required

PeriodUnit.description_en:
Specify whether the subscription-based instance is annual or monthly. Options:

- `Year`: Annual
- `Month`: Monthly

This parameter is required when `ChargeType` is set to `Prepaid`.

Port.description_en:
Set the port number for the private network connection address of the new instance. Value range: 1000~65535.
* If this parameter is left blank, the instance's private network connection address uses port 3717 by default.
* After the instance is created, you can modify the port number of the connection address via the [ModifyDBEndpointPort](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/modifydbendpointport) API. For more details about modifying the port number, see [Modify Port Number](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/modifying_ports).

ProjectName.description_en:
Select the project to which the instance belongs. If this parameter is left blank, the new instance will be added to the default project.
A project is a virtual concept that includes a group of resources, users, and roles. Projects allow unified viewing and management of a group of resources, and control user and role permissions for these resources within the project. For more details, see [Resource Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6649/94333).

RuleCode.description_en: Promotion discount information; temporary support; will be removed in the next version

ShardNumber.description_en:
Number of shards in the sharded cluster. Value range: 2–32.
This parameter is required when the instance type is a sharded cluster (that is, when `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`).

StorageSpaceGB.description_en:
Total storage space for a replica set instance, or storage space for a single Shard in a sharded cluster. Unit: GiB, increment: 10.
* If the instance type is a sharded cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`), after creation, the total capacity of the instance equals the storage space of a single Shard multiplied by the number of Shards.
* You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view MongoDB instance specifications, including storage space specifications supported by different nodes.

StorageType.description_en: Storage type for the instance. Currently, only local SSD disks (i.e., `LocalSSD`) are supported.

SubnetId.description_en:
Subnet ID.
You can call the [DescribeSubnets](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSubnets) API to query the list of subnets under a specified VPC, including subnet IDs.

SuperAccountName.description_en: Database account name. Currently, only the super administrator account can be set when creating an instance, and the account name is fixed as `root`.

SuperAccountPassword.description_en:
Password for the root account. The password must meet the following requirements:

* Can only contain uppercase and lowercase letters, digits, and the following special characters: `_#!@$%^&*()+=-`
* Must be 8–32 characters in length
* Must include at least three of the following: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, or special characters
* Weak passwords that are easily cracked (such as `Admin@123`) are not allowed

* If this parameter is left blank, no password will be set for the root account. The system will automatically generate a password for the root account to ensure instance security
* You can also change the root account password after instance creation using the [ResetDBAccount](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/resetdbaccount) API
* If you use special characters in the password, you may need to escape them when connecting to the instance. For more details, see [Special Characters That Need Escaping](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/account-and-permission#%E5%BD%93%E8%BF%9E%E6%8E%A5%E4%B8%B2%E4%B8%AD%E8%B4%A6%E5%8F%B7%E5%AF%86%E7%A0%81%E5%8C%85%E5%90%AB%E4%BA%86%E7%89%B9%E6%AE%8A%E5%AD%97%E7%AC%A6%E6%97%B6%EF%BC%8C%E4%B8%BA%E4%BD%95%E4%BC%9A%E5%AF%BC%E8%87%B4%E8%BF%9E%E6%8E%A5%E5%A4%B1%E8%B4%A5%EF%BC%9F)
* For details about prohibited weak passwords in MongoDB, see the [Weak Password List](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/account-overview%E5%BC%B1%E5%AF%86%E7%A0%81%E5%88%97%E8%A1%A8)

Tags.description_en:
Array object of tag keys and tag values to bind.
Leaving this parameter blank means the new instance will not bind any tags.

	- If `ListOver` is `false`, there are more logs matching your query that have not been loaded. Call DescribeNormalLogs again and use the `Context` value from the previous response to continue retrieving the remaining logs.
	- If `ListOver` is `true`, all logs matching your query have been loaded.

Keys.description_en:

- If you do not enter any keywords, the log search results will not be filtered by keywords

  For example, setting the search keywords to `"Keys":"warning error"` will return logs that contain either `warning` or `error`
- The maximum length for a log search query is 4 KiB. In addition to the `Keys` parameter, the query may include system-defined fields. To improve search efficiency and accuracy, we recommend not entering too many keywords
- Reserved keywords are not supported for search. For more information about reserved keywords, see [Log Search Reserved Keywords](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/log-overview#%E6%97%A5%E5%BF%97%E6%A3%80%E7%B4%A2%E9%A2%84%E7%95%99%E5%85%B3%E9%94%AE%E8%AF%8D)

AllowListIds.description_en:
Allowlist ID to be unbound from the instance.

- You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](../6447/100775) API to query all allowlist information in the specified region, including allowlist IDs.
- You can pass multiple allowlist IDs at once, separated by commas (,).
- You cannot pass multiple instance IDs and allowlists at the same time. Each request only allows you to unbind multiple instances from one allowlist, or unbind one instance from multiple allowlists at the same time.

InstanceIds.description_en:
Instance ID to be unbound from the allowlist.

- You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](../6447/100741) API to query basic information for all MongoDB instances in the target region, including instance IDs.
- You can pass multiple instance IDs at once, separated by commas (,).
- You cannot pass multiple instance IDs and allowlists at the same time. Each request only allows you to unbind multiple instances from one allowlist, or unbind one instance from multiple allowlists at the same time.

AllowList.description_en:
Enter an IP address or a CIDR-formatted IP range

- If this field is left blank, no changes will be made to the current whitelist IP addresses
- Each whitelist can contain up to 1,000 IP addresses or CIDR-formatted IP ranges
- Duplicate addresses are not allowed; separate multiple addresses with commas (,)
- Enter `0.0.0.0/0` to allow access from all addresses
- Enter `127.0.0.1` to block access from all addresses
- Enter both `0.0.0.0/0` and `127.0.0.1` to allow access from all addresses
- Enter CIDR `192.168.1.0/24` to allow access from all IP addresses in that subnet
- Enter `192.168.1.1` to allow access only from that IP address

AllowListCategory.description_en:
Whitelist type. Available values:

- `Ordinary` (default): Ordinary whitelist
- `Default`: Default whitelist
Each BytePlus account can set up to one default whitelist per region. When you set a new default whitelist, it automatically replaces the previous one, which then becomes a non-default whitelist. For more details, see [Constraints and limitations](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/product-limit).

AllowListDesc.description_en:
Whitelist remark cannot exceed 200 characters.
- If you do not set this parameter, the original whitelist remark will be cleared by default.
- If you want to keep the original whitelist remark, it is recommended to copy it as the value for `AllowListDesc`.
  For example, if the original remark is `test-desc` and you want to retain it, set `"AllowListDesc": "test-desc"` in the request parameters when calling the ModifyAllowList API.

AllowListId.description_en:
Allowlist ID

You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describeallowlists) API to query all allowlist list information for a specific region, including allowlist IDs.

AllowListName.description_en:
Allowlist name

- To modify the IP addresses in an existing allowlist, enter the original allowlist name. You can use the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describeallowlists) API to view all allowlists in a specific region, including their names.
- To change the allowlist name, enter a new name. The name must meet the following requirements:
  - Cannot start with a number or hyphen (-)
  - Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)
  - Must be 1–128 characters long

ApplyInstanceNum.description_en:
Number of instances currently associated with the whitelist

- This parameter is required when you need to modify the `AllowList` parameter
- The value you provide must match the number of instances currently associated with the whitelist; otherwise, an error will occur when calling this API
- You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describeallowlists) API to query all whitelist information in a specified region, including the total number of instances associated with each whitelist (returned as the `AssociatedInstanceNum` parameter)

ModifyMode.description_en:
Modification mode. The available options are as follows:

- `Cover` (default): Use the IP addresses entered in the `AllowList` parameter to overwrite the original whitelist.
- `Append`: Add the IP addresses entered in the `AllowList` parameter to the original whitelist.
- `Delete`: Remove the IP addresses entered in the `AllowList` parameter from the original whitelist. At least one IP address must be retained.

Port.description_en:
Port number after modification. Valid range: 1000–65535.
- You can only modify the port number of the connection address for Mongos nodes in replica set or sharded cluster instances. The effective scope of the new port varies by instance or component type. For details on the effective scope, see [Modify Port Number](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/modifying_ports#%E6%B3%A8%E6%84%8F%E4%BA%8B%E9%A1%B9).
- Changing the port will affect access to some services for a short time. Proceed with caution.
- After changing the port, existing connections will be disconnected. Update your client connection information promptly and use the new port to connect to the instance. For details on how to connect to the instance using Mongo Shell, see [Connect to Instance Using Mongo Shell](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/connect-instance-via-mongo-shell).

- `false`: Disable public network resolution

AutoBackup.description_en: Automatic backup is enabled by default and cannot be disabled. This parameter is always set to `Enable`.

DataBackupRetentionDay.description_en:
Backup retention days (range: 7–365)
If left blank, the instance's backup retention days will not be changed.

DataFullBackupPeriods.description_en:

- `MONDAY`: Monday
- `TUESDAY`: Tuesday
- `WEDNESDAY`: Wednesday
- `THURSDAY`: Thursday
- `FRIDAY`: Friday
- `SATURDAY`: Saturday
- `SUNDAY`: Sunday

- For security reasons, you must select at least two days for the backup cycle. Separate multiple backup days with commas (,).
- If this parameter is left blank, the backup cycle for the instance will not be changed.

DataFullBackupTime.description_en:

- You can set backups to run at any whole hour of the day, with a 1-hour interval.
- If this parameter is left blank, the backup execution time for the instance will not be changed.

BackupId.description_en:
Backup ID required to obtain the backup file download URL

Only backups created using the physical backup method require the ModifyDBInstanceBackupURL API to get the backup file download URL. You can use the [DescribeBackups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describebackups) API to query backup file IDs for a specific instance. In the response, find backup files that meet all of the following conditions:

- Backup status is Success (`BackupStatus` = `Success`)
- Backup type is Physical (`BackupType` = `Physical`)
- Backup download status is NotDownLoad (`BackupDownloadStatus` = `NotDownLoad`)

InstanceId.description_en:

- `false` (default): Auto-renewal is disabled
- `true`: Auto-renewal is enabled

This parameter is only effective when `ChargeType` is set to `Prepaid`

ChargeType.description_en:
Modified instance billing type. Available options:
- `PostPaid`: Pay-as-you-go (also known as postpaid)
- `Prepaid`: Subscription (also known as prepaid)

For more information about billing types, see [Billing Types](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/billing-method).

InstanceIds.description_en:

- Call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describedbinstances) API to view basic information for all MongoDB instances in the target region, including instance IDs
- You can enter multiple instance IDs, separated by English commas (,), to convert them to annual/monthly subscription in bulk
- You can enter up to 10 instance IDs at a time; duplicate IDs are not allowed

Period.description_en:

- When `PeriodUnit` is `Year`, `Period` can be set to 1–3
- When `PeriodUnit` is `Month`, `Period` can be set to 1–9

This parameter is required when `ChargeType` is set to `Prepaid`

PeriodUnit.description_en:

- `Year`: Yearly
- `Month`: Monthly

This parameter is required when `ChargeType` is set to `Prepaid`.
