PointPrefix.description_en: Backup point base path; backuppointinfo returns this field, which may be empty

PointStartTime.description_en: Specifies the channeldate of the backup point. It is used as a new parameter in openapi, with the same function and assignment as BasicChannelDate.

BackupPointId.description_en:
Backup file backup ID. Fuzzy search supported.
* This parameter is valid only when the query scope is the current account (`Scope` is set to `AccountInstances`).
* If this parameter is left blank, backup ID filtering is not applied.

BackupPointName.description_en:
Backup name, supports fuzzy search.
* When the backup query scope is a single instance (that is, when `Scope` is set to `OneInstance`), this parameter is not applicable.
* If this parameter is left blank, the backup name will not be used for filtering.

BackupStrategyList.description_en:
Backup method list. The value range is as follows:

* `ManualBackup`: Manual backup
* `AutomatedBackup`: Automated backup

* Multiple backup methods can be specified at the same time, separated by commas (,).
* If this parameter is left blank, backup method filtering is not applied.

EndTime.description_en:
Query end time. Format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (UTC).
* If a query start time (`StartTime`) is set, this parameter is required.
* The query end time must be later than the start time.
* If this parameter is left blank, time range filtering is not applied.

InstanceId.description_en:
Instance ID.
* When the backup query scope is a single instance (`Scope` is set to `OneInstance`), this parameter is required.
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstances) API to query basic information for all Redis instances in the target region, including instance IDs.
* If this parameter is left blank, instance ID filtering is not applied.

OrderBy.description_en: Sorting basis. Value: string value of OrderBy_E. Currently, only StartTime and InstanceId are supported, replacing the previous constants

OrderType.description_en: Sort order. Value: string value of enum OrderType_E, replaces the original constant

PageNumber.description_en:
Page number for the backup set information list. The value must not exceed the maximum value of the Integer data type. The starting value is 1.
* If this parameter is set, the number of records per page (`PageSize`) is also required.
* If this parameter is left blank, page range filtering is not applied.

PageSize.description_en:
Records per page. Value: integer between 1 and 1000.
* If a page number (`PageNumber`) is set, this parameter is required.
* If this parameter is left blank, records per page will not be used for filtering.

ProjectName.description_en:
Project to which the backup belongs.
* This parameter is only applicable when the query scope is the current account (that is, when `Scope` is set to `AccountInstances`).
* If this parameter is left blank, the project name will not be used for filtering.

Scope.description_en:

* `OneInstance` (default): Query backups within a single instance.
* `AccountInstances`: Query backups under the current account.

Query start time. Format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (UTC).
* If this parameter is set, the query end time (`EndTime`) parameter is also required.
* If this parameter is left blank, time range filtering is not applied.

Status.description_en:

* `Creating`: Creating
* `Available`: Available
* `Unavailable`: Unavailable
* `Deleting`: Deleting

For more information about backup status, see [Backup Status](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/view-backup#%E5%A4%87%E4%BB%BD%E7%8A%B6%E6%80%81).

* `string`
* `list`
* `set`
* `zset`
* `hash`

Leave this parameter blank to disable data type filtering

OrderBy.description_en:
Specify the sorting criteria for query results. The following options are supported:

* `ValueSize` (default): Sorts large key query results by memory usage
* `ValueLen`: Sorts large key query results by number of elements

OrderType.description_en: Optional. Sort order: desc or asc. Default is desc

QueryEndTime.description_en:

* The end time must be later than the start time, and the time range cannot exceed 24 hours

QueryStartTime.description_en:
Query start time, format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (UTC)
* You can view the distribution of large keys for up to the past 15 days
* If this parameter is left blank, the actual query start time defaults to 24 hours before the current time
  For example, if the current time is March 27, 2023, 16:30:00, and `QueryStartTime` is not set, the actual query start time will be March 26, 2023, 16:30:00
* The query end time must be later than the query start time, and the time range cannot exceed 24 hours

ExcludeCompleted.description_en:
Whether to query blue-green deployment tasks that are already completed (including switchover completed `SWITCHOVER_COMPLETED` and delete completed `DELETE_COMPLETED`). Value options are as follows:

* `false` (default): Do not query
* `true`: Query

Instance ID.
You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstances) API to query basic information for all Redis instances in the target region, including the instance ID.

ArchType.description_en:
Architecture type of the Redis instance. Available options:

* `Cluster`: Enables sharded cluster (number of shards greater than 1)
* `Standard`: Does not enable sharded cluster (number of shards is 1)

* If this parameter is left blank, architecture type will not be used as a filtering condition
* For more information about product architecture, see [Product Architecture](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/product-component-architecture)

InstanceClass.description_en:
Type of Redis instance. Available values:

* `PrimarySecondary`: Primary-secondary instance
* `Standalone`: Single-node instance

* Leave this parameter blank to ignore instance type when filtering
* For more information about instance types, see [Product Architecture](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/product-component-architecture)

ChargeType.description_en:
Instance billing type. Valid values:

* `PostPaid`: Pay-as-you-go
* `PrePaid`: Subscription (annual/monthly)

* If this parameter is left blank, instance billing type will not be used to filter instances
* For more information about billing types, see [Billing Types](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/pay-as-you-go)

DataLayout.description_en:
Instance data storage type.



* This parameter is only relevant for Enterprise Edition instances (i.e., `ServiceType` is `Enterprise`); Community Edition instances (i.e., `ServiceType` is `Basic`) do not involve data storage type, and `DataLayout` is always set to `RAM`
* If this parameter is left blank, data storage type will not be used to filter instances

EngineVersion.description_en:
Database version of the instance. Valid values:

* `5.0`
* `6.0`
* `7.0`


If this parameter is left empty, the database version condition will not be used for filtering.

FilterByTags.description_en: Adapt Tag Editor for Tag Search

InstanceId.description_en:
Instance ID. Exact match.
If this parameter is left empty, the instance ID condition will not be used for filtering.

InstanceIds.description_en: Batch Instance ID Fuzzy Search

InstanceName.description_en:
Instance name. Fuzzy search is supported.
If this parameter is left empty, the instance name condition will not be used for filtering.

InstanceNames.description_en: Used for bulk instance name fuzzy search

PageNumber.description_en: Page number of the instance information list. Must not exceed the maximum value of the Integer data type. The starting and default value is 1.

PageSize.description_en: Number of records per page. Must be an integer between 1 and 1000. Default is 10.

ProjectName.description_en:
Project name to which the instance belongs.
If this parameter is left empty, the project name condition will not be used for filtering.

RegionId.description_en:
Region ID to which the instance belongs.
* If this parameter is left empty, the region set in the signature will be used by default. For more information about the signature mechanism, see [Signature Mechanism](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/signature-mechanism).
* You can call the [DescribeRegions](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describeregions) API to query all supported region information for Redis instances, including region IDs.

ServiceType.description_en:
Service type of the instance. Valid values:

* `Basic` (default): Community Edition
* `Enterprise`: Enterprise Edition

ShardedCluster.description_en:
Whether the instance has enabled sharded cluster. Valid values:

* `0`: Not enabled
* `1`: Enabled

If this parameter is left empty, the sharded cluster condition will not be used for filtering.

Status.description_en:
Instance status. For more details about instance status, see [Instance Status](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/instance-status).
If this parameter is left blank, instance status will not be used to filter instances

TagFilters.description_en:
Array of tag key-value pairs for query filtering.
If this parameter is left empty, the tag condition will not be used for filtering.

Tags.description_en: Deprecated: OPEAN-API used for tag search

VpcId.description_en:
VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) ID to which the instance belongs. Fuzzy search is supported.
* If this parameter is left empty, the VPC ID condition will not be used for filtering.
* You can call the [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) API to query all VPCs under the current account, including VPC IDs.

VpcIds.description_en: Used for batch fuzzy search of VpcID

ZoneId.description_en:
ID of the availability zone to which the instance belongs. Fuzzy search is supported.
You can call the [DescribeZones](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describezones) API to query the availability zone resource information for Redis instances in the specified region, including the availability zone ID

PageNumber.description_en: Page number for the parameter information list; must not exceed the maximum value of the Integer data type; starts at 1

PageSize.description_en: Records per page (must be an integer between 1 and 100)

DataLayout.description_en:
Data storage types for Redis Enterprise Edition instances: Possible values:

* `RAM`: Memory type
* `Hybrid`: Hybrid type

* If this parameter is left blank, the data storage type condition will not be used as a filter.
* For more information about data storage types in Enterprise Edition instances, see [Data Storage Types](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/84772/1439014#%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE%E5%AD%98%E5%82%A8%E5%BD%A2%E6%80%81).

RegionId.description_en:
Region ID
You can call the [DescribeRegions](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/84772/71730) API to query all available region resources for Redis instances, including region IDs.

Context.description_en:
The context of the Fatlog log query result, used when loading more Fatlog log records.
After calling the DescribeFatLogs API, you can determine whether there are remaining Fatlog log records to load based on the value of the returned parameter `ListOver`:

* If `ListOver` is `false`, there are still Fatlog log records matching the query conditions that have not been loaded. You can call the DescribeFatLogs API again and use the `Context` value returned in the previous API call to view the remaining Fatlog log records.
* If `ListOver` is `true`, all Fatlog log records matching the query conditions have been loaded.

FatLogType.description_en:
Fatlog type. Valid values:

* `proxy`: Proxy node
* `server`: Server node

If no value is specified, the Fatlog type is not set. Both proxy and server logs are returned.

InstanceId.description_en:
Instance ID
You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstances) API to query the basic information of all Redis instances in the target region, including the instance ID.

NodeIds.description_en:
Node ID to query Fatlog logs.
* If this parameter is left empty, the Fatlog log details for all nodes in the target instance are queried by default.
* You can query multiple node IDs at the same time. Separate multiple node IDs with commas (,).
* You can call the [DescribeNodeIds](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describenodeids) API to query all node ID information for the target Redis instance.
* The total length of the `NodeIds` string must not exceed 1024 bytes. It is recommended to query no more than 8 nodes at a time.

PageSize.description_en: Records per page. Value range: 1–1000.

QueryEndTime.description_en:
Query end time, format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (UTC).
* If this parameter is left empty, the actual query end time defaults to the current time.
* The query end time must be later than the query start time.

QueryStartTime.description_en:
Query start time, format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (UTC).
If this parameter is left empty, the actual query start time defaults to 3 days before the current time.
For example, if the current time is March 4, 2026, 16:30:00, and `QueryStartTime` is not specified, the actual query start time is March 1, 2026, 16:30:00.

Context.description_en: Optional. Query context is empty for the first query

KeyType.description_en:
Specify the data type to filter hot key query results. Supported data types:

* `string`
* `list`
* `set`
* `zset`
* `hash`

Leave this parameter blank to not use data type filtering.

OrderBy.description_en: Optional. Sorting criteria, not used yet

OrderType.description_en: Optional. Sort order (not in use yet)

PageSize.description_en: Records per page must be an integer between 1 and 1000

QueryEndTime.description_en:
Query end time, format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (UTC)
* If this parameter is left blank, the query end time defaults to the current time
* The query end time must be later than the query start time, and the time interval cannot exceed 15 days

QueryStartTime.description_en:
Query start time, format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (UTC)
* You can view hot Key distribution for up to the past 15 days
* If this parameter is left blank, the actual query start time defaults to one hour before the current time
  For example, if the current time is 2023-03-27 16:30:00 and `QueryStartTime` is not set, the actual query start time will be 2023-03-27 15:30:00
* The query end time must be later than the query start time, and the time range cannot exceed 15 days

ShardIds.description_en:
Specify the list of shard IDs used to filter hot key query results.
* You can provide up to 40 shard IDs at a time, separated by commas (,).
* Leave this parameter blank to disable shard ID filtering.
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceShards](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstanceshards) API to view details of each shard in the target Redis instance, including the shard ID (shown as the `ShardId` field in the response).

* `CreateTime` (default): Sort by task creation time
* `StartTime`: Sort by task start time
* `FinishTime`: Sort by task completion time

OrderType.description_en:

Sort order. Available values:

* `DESC` (default): descending order
* `ASC`: ascending order

ParameterGroupId.description_en:
Parameter Template ID
You can call the [DescribeParameterGroups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describeparametergroups) API to view basic information about all parameter templates under your account and region, including the parameter template ID

EngineVersion.description_en:
Applicable Redis database versions for the parameter template

* `7.0`: Redis 7.0
* `6.0`: Redis 6.0
* `5.0`: Redis 5.0

If this parameter is left blank, the database version will not be used as a filtering condition for the parameter template.

PageNumber.description_en: Page number for the parameter template information list. Value must not exceed the maximum for the Integer data type. The starting value is always 1.

PageSize.description_en: Records per page: Enter an integer between 1 and 100

Source.description_en:
Parameter template creation source. Possible values:

* `User`: Created by the user (custom template)
* `System`: Created by the system (system template)

Leave this field empty to ignore the creation source when filtering parameter templates

InstanceId.description_en:
Instance ID
You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstances) API to query basic information about all Redis instances in the target region, including the instance ID.

MaxStartTime.description_en:
Latest execution time for scheduled events to query. Format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (UTC)
* Leave this parameter blank to skip filtering by latest scheduled execution time
* The end time must be later than the start time

MinStartTime.description_en:
The earliest execution time of the scheduled events to be queried. Format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (UTC)
If this parameter is left empty, the earliest scheduled execution time will not be used for filtering

PageNumber.description_en: Page number for the scheduled event list. Value must not exceed the maximum for the Integer data type. Starts at 1

Region ID.

If this parameter is left empty, all available region resource information under the current account will be returned.

Context.description_en:
Context for slow log query results, used when you need to load more slow log records.
After calling the DescribeSlowLogs API, you can check the value of the returned parameter `ListOver` to see if there are more slow log records to load:

* If `ListOver` is `false`, there are still slow log records matching your query that have not been loaded. You can call the DescribeSlowLogs API again and use the `Context` value from the previous response to view the remaining slow log records.
* If `ListOver` is `true`, all slow log records matching your query have been loaded.

DBName.description_en:
Database for slow logs
The supported database values vary by slow log type:

* Proxy node slow logs: Any integer from 0 to 256
* Server node slow logs: Since the database is empty for server node slow logs, only '-' is supported

If this parameter is left blank, slow logs from all databases are returned by default

Instance ID

Node ID(s) required for slow log query

* You can enter multiple node IDs separated by commas (,)
* To view all node IDs for the target Redis instance, call the [DescribeNodeIds](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describenodeids) API

Query end time, format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (UTC)

* The query end time must be later than the query start time

QueryStartTime.description_en:
Query start time, format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (UTC)
If this parameter is left blank, the actual query start time defaults to three days before the current time.
For example, if the current time is August 1, 2022, 16:30:00, and `QueryStartTime` is not set, the actual query start time will be July 29, 2022, 16:30:00.

SlowLogType.description_en:
Type of slow log. Valid values:

* `Server`: Slow log for Server node
* `Proxy`: Slow log for Proxy node

* If this parameter is left empty, slow logs for all node types are returned by default
* If both `NodeIds` and `SlowLogType` are provided, `NodeIds` takes precedence

InstanceIds.description_en:
You need to query instance IDs with bound tags.
* You can enter multiple instance IDs at once, separated by English commas (,). Up to 50 instance IDs can be entered at the same time.
* To view basic information for all Redis instances in a specific region, including instance IDs, call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstances) API.

PageNumber.description_en: Page number for the instance tag information list. Value must not exceed the maximum value of the Integer data type and starts at 1

PageSize.description_en: Records per page, range: 1–1000

TagFilters.description_en:
Array of tag key-value pairs for query filtering
Leave this parameter empty to disable tag-based filtering

CreationEndTime.description_en:
End time of the time range for querying by task creation time, in the format `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (UTC).
If `TaskId` is not specified, both `CreationStartTime` and `CreationEndTime` must be provided.

CreationStartTime.description_en:
Start time for querying based on task creation time, in the format `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (UTC).
If `TaskId` is not specified, you must provide both `CreationStartTime` and `CreationEndTime`.

InstanceName.description_en: Instance Name

PageNumber.description_en: Task list page number. Must be an integer greater than or equal to 1.

PageSize.description_en: Number of records per page. Must be an integer between 1 and 100.

ProjectName.description_en: Project name.

TaskId.description_en:
Task ID. Used to query a specific task.
If `TaskId` is not specified, you must provide both `CreationStartTime` and `CreationEndTime`.

RegionId.description_en:
Region ID
You can call the [DescribeRegions](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describeregions) API to query all available region resource information for Redis instances, including region IDs

AllowListIds.description_en:
Enter the whitelist ID(s) you want to unbind from the instance
* You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describeallowlists) API to view all whitelist information in a specified region, including whitelist IDs
* You can enter multiple whitelist IDs at once, separated by commas (,)
* You cannot enter multiple instance IDs and whitelist IDs at the same time. Each operation allows you to unbind multiple instances from a single whitelist, or unbind a single instance from multiple whitelists

ClientToken.description_en: Ensures request idempotency and prevents duplicate request submissions. The client generates this parameter value, which must be unique across different requests, case-sensitive, and no longer than 127 ASCII characters.

InstanceIds.description_en:
Instance IDs that need to be unbound from the whitelist.
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstances) API to view basic information for all Redis instances in the target region, including instance IDs.
* You can enter multiple instance IDs at once, separated by English commas (,).
* Each operation only allows you to either unbind multiple instances from one whitelist, or unbind one instance from multiple whitelists at once.

ApplyImmediately.description_en:
Whether to execute the configuration change immediately. Value options:

* `true`: Change immediately.
* `false`: Change during the maintenance window.

For more information about maintenance windows, see [Set Maintenance Window](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/set-maintenance-period).

ClientToken.description_en: Used to ensure request idempotency and prevent duplicate submissions. This parameter value is generated by the client and must be unique across different requests, case-sensitive, and no longer than 127 ASCII characters.

ConfigureNodes.description_en:
Configure the list of availability zones for the node.
If this parameter is left blank, the node's availability zone will not be modified.

InstanceId.description_en:
Instance ID.
You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstances) API to query basic information for all Redis instances in the target region, including instance IDs.

MultiAZ.description_en:
Configure the instance's availability zone deployment scheme. Value options:

* `disabled`: Single availability zone deployment scheme.
* `enabled`: Multi-availability zone deployment scheme.

* If this parameter is left blank, the instance's availability zone deployment scheme will not be modified.
* For more information about availability zone deployment schemes, see [Multi-Availability Zone Disaster Recovery Solution](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/multi-az-solution).

NodeNumber.description_en:
Number of nodes in each shard. Value range: 2–6.
By default, each account can create up to 4 nodes of 256 MiB specification (that is, `ShardCapacity` value is `256`) in each region. If you need to adjust the purchase quota for 256 MiB nodes (maximum 10), see [Account Quota](https://vsop-online.bytedance.net/doc/manage/detail/6293/6293/71560#%E8%B4%A6%E5%8F%B7%E9%85%8D%E9%A2%9D).

ShardCapacity.description_en:
Memory capacity per shard, in MiB. The available values are as follows:

* If the instance does not enable sharded cluster (that is, `ShardedCluster` is set to `0`), the selectable memory capacity per shard is: 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 24576, 65536.
* If the instance enables sharded cluster (that is, `ShardedCluster` is set to `1`), the selectable memory capacity per shard is: 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384.

* If this parameter is left blank, the instance memory capacity will not be modified.
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API to query details of the specified instance, including whether sharding is enabled and the memory capacity of each shard.
* If you need to reduce shard capacity, ensure that the instance's current **used memory** does not exceed the new total memory capacity, where new total memory capacity = updated memory per shard x number of shards. For information on **used memory**, see [View Instance Information](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/view-instance).
* Each instance specification supports corresponding shard capacity and bandwidth. When you modify shard capacity, the bandwidth and specification will also be updated accordingly. For more details about Redis instance specifications, see [Product Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/product-specification).

ShardNumber.description_en:
Number of shards in the instance. Value range: 2–256.
* This parameter is required only when sharded cluster is enabled (that is, `ShardedCluster` value is `1`).
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API to query details of the specified instance, including whether sharding is enabled and the number of shards.
* To reduce the number of shards, ensure the instance's current **used memory** does not exceed the new total memory capacity, where new total memory capacity = memory per shard after change × number of shards. For information on **used memory**, see [View Instance Information](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/view-instance).
* If the single-node instance before the change is a sharded cluster instance and has applied for a direct connection address, then when changing to a primary/standby instance, the number of shards cannot exceed 8. If you need to increase the number of shards in the scenario where direct connection address is enabled, please [submit a ticket](https://console.volcengine.com/workorder/create/) to contact technical support.

ShardedCluster.description_en:
Whether to enable sharded cluster. The available values are:

* `0`: Disabled
* `1`: Enabled

If the single-node instance before the change is already a sharded cluster instance and has applied for a direct connection address, you cannot select 'Disabled' when changing to a primary-secondary instance.

ApplyImmediately.description_en:
Choose whether to apply configuration changes immediately. Available options:

* `true`: Apply changes immediately
* `false`: Apply changes during the maintenance window

For more information about the maintenance window, see [Set Maintenance Window](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/set-maintenance-period).

BackupPointName.description_en:
Set a backup name for the full backup created before the change. If you do not specify a backup name, the backup ID is used by default.

To set a backup name, make sure it meets all of the following requirements:

* Starts with a Chinese character, letter, or underscore (_)
* Contains 1–128 characters
* Includes only Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)

This parameter is effective only if you choose to create a backup before the change (that is, when `CreateBackup` is set to `true`).

ClientToken.description_en: Ensures request idempotency and prevents duplicate submissions. The client generates this parameter value, which must be unique across requests, case-sensitive, and no longer than 127 ASCII characters

CreateBackup.description_en:
Whether to create a full backup before making changes. Valid values:

* `true`: Create a backup
* `false` (default): Do not create a backup

* This parameter applies only to primary-secondary instances (`InstanceClass` set to `PrimarySecondary`). Single-node instances (`InstanceClass` set to `Standalone`) do not support backup, so you do not need to set this parameter.
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API to query details of a specified instance, including its type.

InstanceId.description_en:
Instance ID
You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstances) API to query basic information about all Redis instances in the target region, including the instance ID

ShardCapacity.description_en:
Memory capacity per shard, in MiB. Valid values: 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384.
* If this parameter is not specified, the original single-shard capacity will be used as the `ShardCapacity` after enabling the sharded cluster. However, the supported single-shard capacity specifications differ between non-sharded and sharded cluster instances. If you use a single-shard capacity not supported by sharded cluster instances, an error will occur when calling this API. For more details about Redis instance specifications, see [Product Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/product-specification).
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API to query details of a specified instance, including the memory capacity of each shard.
* To reduce shard capacity, ensure that the current used memory of the instance does not exceed 85% of the new total memory capacity (total capacity = single-shard capacity x number of shards).
* Each instance specification has corresponding supported shard capacity and bandwidth. Therefore, when you modify the shard capacity of an instance, its bandwidth and specification will also be updated accordingly. For more details about Redis instance specifications, see [Product Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/product-specification).

ShardNumber.description_en: Number of shards in the instance. Range: 2–256

ShardedCluster.description_en:
Whether to enable sharded cluster. Available values:

* `0`: Not enabled
* `1`: Enabled

Currently, only instances with sharded cluster not enabled can be changed to enabled. Therefore, the value must be `1`.

ClientToken.description_en: Ensures request idempotency and prevents duplicate submissions. The client generates this parameter value, which must be unique across requests, case-sensitive, and no longer than 127 ASCII characters.

EventId.description_en:
Event ID of the scheduled event to execute immediately. Only scheduled events with a status of Waiting (i.e., `Status` value is `Waiting`) can be executed immediately.
You can call the [DescribePlannedEvents](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describeplannedevents) API to query scheduled event information for the target Redis instance within a specified time period, including event ID and event status.

ClientToken.description_en: Ensures request idempotency and prevents duplicate submissions. The client must generate this parameter value, which must be unique for each request, case-sensitive, and no longer than 127 ASCII characters.

InstanceId.description_en:
Instance ID
You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstances) API to query basic information for all Redis instances in the target region, including the instance ID

ApplyImmediately.description_en:
Apply configuration changes immediately? Available options:

* `true`: Apply changes now
* `false`: Apply changes during the maintenance window

For more information about the maintenance window, see [Set Maintenance Window](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/set-maintenance-period).

BackupPointName.description_en:
Set a backup name for the full backup created before the change. The backup name must meet all of the following requirements:

* Setting CIDR `192.168.1.0/24` allows access from all IP addresses in that subnet; setting `192.168.1.1` allows access only from that IP address

AllowListCategory.description_en:

* `Default`: Default whitelist

Each BytePlus account can set up to one default whitelist per region. When you set a new default whitelist, it automatically replaces the previous default whitelist, which will become a non-default whitelist. For more details, see [Constraints and limitations](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/quota-and-limit#%E5%8A%9F%E8%83%BD%E7%89%B9%E6%80%A7%E9%99%90%E5%88%B6).

* You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describeallowlists) API to query all whitelist information under your account in the specified region, including the total number of instances bound to each whitelist (shown as the `AssociatedInstanceNum` parameter in the response).

RoleName.description_en:

* `Administrator`: Allows all supported commands on all Keys for all Redis instances
* `ReadWrite`: Allows all commands except those in the `admin` category on all Keys
* `ReadOnly`: Allows all commands in the `read` category on all Keys
* `NotDangerous`: Allows all commands except those in the `dangerous` category on all Keys
* `NotWrite`: Allows all commands except those in the `write` category on all Keys

* If this parameter is left empty, the account role will not be changed.
* The role of the default account is fixed as `Administrator` and cannot be changed.
* For details on the specific commands supported by each role's ACL rules, see [ACL Syntax](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/create-role#acl-%E8%AF%AD%E6%B3%95).

AdditionalBandwidth.description_en:
Set additional read and write bandwidth for a single shard. After setting, the additional read and write bandwidth for the single shard will both be the specified value. Unit: MB/s.
* It is recommended to use the `AdditionalWriteBandwidth` and `AdditionalReadBandwidth` parameters to set additional read and write bandwidth for a single shard.
* If `AdditionalWriteBandwidth` or `AdditionalReadBandwidth` is not set, the value specified by `AdditionalBandwidth` will be used as the additional read and write bandwidth for the single shard.

AdditionalReadBandwidth.description_en:
Set the additional read bandwidth for a single shard. This is the extra read bandwidth added on top of the default bandwidth, measured in MB/s.
The value for additional read bandwidth must meet all of the following conditions:

* Must be greater than or equal to 0. If set to 0, no additional read bandwidth is added, and the single shard bandwidth equals the default read bandwidth.
* The sum of the additional read bandwidth and the default bandwidth cannot exceed the maximum bandwidth modification limit allowed for the current instance. For more details about bandwidth limits, see [Bandwidth modification range](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/modify-bandwidth#%E5%B8%A6%E5%AE%BD%E4%BF%AE%E6%94%B9%E8%8C%83%E5%9B%B4).
* **The total bandwidth for a Redis instance cannot exceed 2.5 GB/s.** Therefore, the maximum bandwidth for the instance = min[(number of shards × maximum single shard bandwidth), 2.5 GB/s]. For more details, see [Bandwidth description](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/product-specification#%E5%B8%A6%E5%AE%BD%E8%AF%B4%E6%98%8E).

AdditionalWriteBandwidth.description_en:
Set the additional write bandwidth for a single shard. This is the extra write bandwidth added on top of the default bandwidth, measured in MB/s.
Additional write bandwidth must meet all of the following conditions:

* Must be greater than or equal to 0. If set to 0, no extra write bandwidth is added, and the single shard bandwidth equals the default write bandwidth.
* The sum of additional write bandwidth and default bandwidth cannot exceed the maximum bandwidth allowed for the current instance. For more details about bandwidth limits, see [Bandwidth Modification Range](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/modify-bandwidth#%E5%B8%A6%E5%AE%BD%E4%BF%AE%E6%94%B9%E8%8C%83%E5%9B%B4).
* **The total bandwidth for a Redis instance cannot exceed 2.5 GB/s**. Therefore, the maximum bandwidth for the instance = min[(number of shards × maximum single shard bandwidth), 2.5 GB/s]. For more details, see [Bandwidth Description](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/product-specification#%E5%B8%A6%E5%AE%BD%E8%AF%B4%E6%98%8E).

* If you need to reduce shard capacity, make sure the current used memory of the instance does not exceed 85% of the new total memory capacity (total capacity = single shard capacity x number of shards).
* Each instance specification supports corresponding shard capacity and bandwidth. * To reduce the number of shards, ensure that the current used memory does not exceed 85% of the new total memory capacity (total capacity = per-shard capacity × number of shards).

RetentionDays.description_en:
Set the release time for the old IP address. Available options:

* `0`: Release immediately
* `1` (default): Release after 1 day
* `2`: Release after 2 days
* `3`: Release after 3 days
* `7`: Release after 7 days

Modifying a private network or subnet does not change the private network address or direct connection address domain name, but the corresponding IP address will change. It is recommended to clear the client cache before the old IP address is released to avoid read/write errors. For more details, see [Modify Private Network or Subnet](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/modify-vpc-or-subnet).

SubnetId.description_en:
Set the subnet ID for the instance.
* Subnets have an availability zone attribute. You must select a subnet in the target VPC that is in the same availability zone as the instance.
* A subnet is an IP address block within a VPC. All cloud resources in the VPC must be deployed in a subnet. Subnets assign private IP addresses to cloud resources. You can use the [CreateSubnet](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/CreateSubnet) API to create a subnet.
* You can use the [DescribeSubnets](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSubnets) API to view all subnets in a specified availability zone, including their subnet IDs.

VpcId.description_en:
Set the private network ID for the instance
* If you enter the current private network ID of the instance, only the subnet will be changed, and the private network will remain unchanged
* For optimal performance, place the Redis instance and the ECS instance you want to connect to in the same private network. Otherwise, they cannot communicate over the internal network. You can use the [CreateVpc](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/CreateVpc) API to create a private network
* You can use the [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) API to query private network information that meets specified criteria, including the private network ID

AddrType.description_en:
Connection address types that require an address prefix. Available values:

* `Public`: Public address
* `Private`: Private address
* `DirectLink`: DirectLink address

* To modify a DirectLink or public connection address, you must first apply for the corresponding connection address. For details on how to apply for DirectLink and public connection addresses, see [Apply for DirectLink Address](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/apply-direct-connection-address) and [Enable Public Access](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/apply-public-address).
* For more information about Redis connection addresses, see [Connection Address Types](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/view-address#%E8%BF%9E%E6%8E%A5%E5%9C%B0%E5%9D%80%E7%B1%BB%E5%9E%8B)

NewAddressPrefix.description_en:
Modified connection address prefix. The connection address prefix must meet all of the following requirements:

* Consists of lowercase letters, numbers, or hyphens (-)
* Starts with a letter and ends with a letter or number
* Length is 8 to 53 characters
* The modified connection address must be globally unique and cannot duplicate any connection address in any region of Volcengine

* If this parameter is left blank, the connection address prefix will not be modified
* If you need to upgrade the domain suffix (that is, `UpgradeRegionDomain` is `true`), you must also provide the connection address prefix (`NewAddressPrefix` cannot be empty)
* If you do not need to upgrade the domain suffix (that is, `UpgradeRegionDomain` is `false`), you must modify at least one of the `NewAddressPrefix` or `NewPort` parameters
* After modifying the connection address, existing connections will be disconnected. Please update your client connection information promptly and use the new connection address to connect to the instance. For details on how to connect to an instance, see [Connect to Instance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/connect-to-instance)
* Currently, only the connection address prefix can be modified, which is the part before `redis.ivolces.com` or `redis.volces.com`. For more information, see [Modify Connection Address](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/modify-address)

NewPort.description_en:
Modified connection address port number. Supported port ranges vary by address type:

* Private and public addresses support ports in the range 1024–65535
* Direct connection addresses support ports in the ranges 1024–4000 and 5100–64512

* If this parameter is left blank, the port number of the connection address will not be changed
* If you do not need to upgrade the domain suffix (that is, `UpgradeRegionDomain` is `false`), you must modify at least one of the `NewAddressPrefix` or `NewPort` parameters
* After modifying the connection address or port number, existing connections will be disconnected. Please update your client connection settings promptly and use the new port number to connect to the instance. For details on how to connect to an instance, see [Connect to Instance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/connect-to-instance)
* Changing the port may temporarily affect access to some services. Proceed with caution. For more information, see [Modify Port Number](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/modify-port)

UpgradeRegionDomain.description_en:
Whether to upgrade the domain suffix of the connection address. Valid values:

* `true`: Upgrade
* `false` (default): Do not upgrade

* If you want to upgrade the domain suffix (that is, set `UpgradeRegionDomain` to `true`), you must also provide the connection address prefix (`NewAddressPrefix` cannot be empty)
* After upgrading the domain suffix, existing connections will be disconnected. Update your client connection settings promptly and use the new connection address to connect to the instance. For details on how to connect to an instance, see [Connect to Instance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/connect-to-instance)
* Once the domain suffix is upgraded, you cannot revert to the original suffix. Proceed with caution
* The upgraded domain suffix will automatically include the region information of the instance. The domain suffix will change from `redis.ivolces.com` (or `redis.volces.com`) to `redis.{Region ID}.ivolces.com` (or `redis.{Region ID}.volces.com`). The old connection address will be retained for 12 hours and will be automatically released after the retention period expires. For more details, see [Upgrade Domain Suffix](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/upgrade-domain-suffix)

BackupPointName.description_en:

* Starts with a Chinese character, letter, or underscore (_)
* Length is 1–128 characters
* May only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)

* This parameter is only effective if you choose to create a full backup before the change (that is, when `CreateBackup` is set to `true`)
* If you do not set a backup name, the backup ID will be used as the default name

FlashPerShard.description_en:

The valid range for this parameter depends on the instance's data storage type:

* For hybrid instances (DataLayout set to `Hybrid`): 10240–30720 MiB (10–30 GiB), with increments of 10240 MiB (10 GiB)
* For memory instances (DataLayout set to `RAM`): Must be 0; high-speed storage capacity is not supported

* You can call the [DescribeEnterpriseDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/84772/1168033) API to view details of your target Redis Enterprise Edition instance, including its data storage type
* For more information about data storage types in Enterprise Edition instances, see [Data Storage Type](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/84772/1258077#%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE%E5%AD%98%E5%82%A8%E5%BD%A2%E6%80%81)

Set the maintenance window range for the instance in the format `HH:mm-HH:mm` (UTC+8).
* For the maintenance window you enter, the start time's `mm` must be `00` and the end time's `mm` must be `59`. For example, you can set the maintenance window to `00:00-01:59`.
* To ensure tasks run properly during the maintenance window, the interval between the start and end times must be at least 2 hours and no more than 24 hours.

You can call the [DescribeParameterGroups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describeparametergroups) API to view basic information for all parameter templates under your account and region, including the template name.
* To change the parameter template name, enter a new name directly. The name must meet all of the following requirements:

   * Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)

* `Inc`: Restore using backup files created with the `Inc` (incremental backup) method. This restores by point in time.

* To restore by point in time (`BackupType` set to `Inc`), you must enable the data flashback feature first. For details, see [Restore to original instance by point in time](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/recovery-by-time-point#%E6%81%A2%E5%A4%8D%E5%88%B0%E5%8E%9F%E5%AE%9E%E4%BE%8B).

* You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstances) API to query basic information for all Redis instances in the target region, including the instance ID.

TargetPrimaryNodeId.description_en:
Replica node ID for master-slave switchover
* The `TargetPrimaryNodeIds` and `TargetPrimaryNodeId` parameters cannot both be empty; if both parameters are set, the value of `TargetPrimaryNodeIds` takes precedence
* The current role of the input node must be replica (that is, `CurrentRole` is `SecondaryNode`)

TargetPrimaryNodeIds.description_en:

* Supports batch switchover for up to 50 shards at the same time
* When performing batch switchover, you can select up to 1 replica node from each shard for switchover
* The `TargetPrimaryNodeIds` and `TargetPrimaryNodeId` parameters cannot both be empty; if both parameters are set, the value of `TargetPrimaryNodeIds` takes precedence
* The current role of the input node must be replica (that is, `CurrentRole` is `SecondaryNode`)

ApplyImmediately.description_en:
Whether to perform the blue-green switchover immediately. The value range is as follows:

* `true`: Switch immediately
* `false`: Switch during the maintenance window

If you choose to switch during the maintenance window, the blue-green deployment enters the **Waiting for Switchover** state, which will persist until the task is completed. For more information about blue-green deployment states, see [Blue-Green Deployment States](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/upgrade_major_version_using_blue_green_deployment#NFCgYsLA). For instructions on setting the maintenance window, see [Set Maintenance Window](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/set-maintenance-period).

FailbackToPrimaryDelayInMinutes.description_en:
Duration of the fault before automatically switching back to the primary availability zone. Unit: minutes. Valid values:

* 5
* 10
* 15

* This parameter only takes effect when simulating a failover for the instance's primary availability zone (that is, the first availability zone returned in the `ZoneIds` field when calling the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API).
* If this parameter is left blank, automatic failback to the primary availability zone will not occur. After failover, the primary node may be located in the secondary availability zone, and the secondary node may be in the primary availability zone. You can manually switch the instance's availability zone after failover by calling the [ModifyDBInstanceAZConfigure](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/modifydbinstanceazconfigure) API.

DestinationConfig.AutoInstallBlkNone.description_en:
Whether to automatically install blk-none on the target instance or target image
Values:
- true: Automatically install
- false: Default value, do not install automatically
Only applies when migrating to Linux cloud server instances or Linux cloud service images

DestinationConfig.AutoInstallVirtio11.description_en:
Whether to automatically install the Virtio1.1 driver for the target instance or target image. Values:
- true: Automatically install
- false: Default value, do not install automatically
Only valid when migrating to Linux cloud server instances or Linux cloud service images

DestinationConfig.AutoReplicate.description_en:
Whether the migration task automatically starts after passing the pre-check. Values:
* false: Default value; does not start migration automatically
* true: Starts migration automatically
Only valid when migrating to cloud server instances or cloud service images

DestinationConfig.DestinationSystem.description_en:
Target operating system. Possible values:
- Unknown: Unknown
- VeLinux10Centos: Indicates migration to veLinux 1.0 CentOS-compatible operating system
- VeLinux20Centos: Indicates migration to veLinux 2.0 CentOS-compatible operating system
This parameter is required when `DestinationConfig.DestinationType` is set to `ECSSystem`

DestinationConfig.DestinationType.description_en:
Target type, values:
- ECSInstance: Cloud server instance
- ECSImage: Cloud server image
- ECSSystem: Cloud server operating system
- ECSTemplate: Create cloud server instance using migration template
The feature to create cloud server instances using migration templates is currently in invite-only testing. To request access, please contact your account manager.

DestinationConfig.ImageName.description_en:
Image Name
- Must start with a letter or Chinese character
- Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), hyphens (-), and periods (.)
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
This parameter is required when migrating to a cloud server image

DestinationConfig.InstanceId.description_en:
Target Instance ID: You can query and obtain it using the [DescribeInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeInstances) API
This parameter is required when migrating to a cloud server instance

DestinationConfig.LicenseType.description_en:
License type
Options:
- VolcanoEngine: Default. Uses the official BytePlus license based on your source server's operating system
- BYOL: Bring your own license (BYOL)

DiskConfigs.N.DestinationDiskSize.description_en:
Target cloud image disk capacity after adjustment (in GiB)
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk number; valid range: 0–14
- Separate multiple disk numbers with `&`
- Supported system disk capacity range: 40 GiB ~ 2048 GiB, and must not be less than the total size of all migration partitions
This parameter is currently in invite-only testing. To request access, please contact your account manager

DiskConfigs.N.DiskIndex.description_en:
Source server disk index, starting from `0`
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk number, valid range: 0–14
- Use `&` to separate multiple disk numbers
The value of parameter - N cannot exceed the actual number of disks on the source server

DiskConfigs.N.DiskSize.description_en:
Source server disk capacity, unit: GiB.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk sequence number, corresponding to the disk sequence number identified by `DiskConfigs.N.DiskIndex`. Value range: 0–14.
- Use `&` to separate multiple disk sequence numbers.
The value of parameter - N cannot exceed the actual number of disks on the source server.

DiskConfigs.N.Partitions.N.AbortPartitio.description_en:
Whether to skip this partition during migration. Values:
* false: Default, do not skip
* true: Skip
* Supported only for Linux file copy migration to 'Cloud Server Image'
* Partitions with mount points `/` and `/boot` must be migrated
* Currently supports system disk only
* The first N: Disk number, value range: 0–14
* The second N: Partition number
* Use & to separate multiple partition configurations
* This parameter is currently in invite-only testing. To request access, please contact your account manager

DiskConfigs.N.Partitions.N.DestinationPa.description_en:
Adjusted target cloud image partition capacity (unit: Bytes)
- The first N: indicates the disk index, range: 0–14
- The second N: indicates the partition index
* Use `&` to separate multiple partition capacities
* The adjusted partition size cannot be smaller than the used space, and the total size of all partitions cannot exceed the disk size
* This parameter is currently in invite-only testing. To request access, please contact your account manager

MigrationJobDescription.description_en:
Task description
- Must start with a letter or Chinese character
- Only Chinese characters, letters, numbers, periods (.), spaces, underscores (_), hyphens (-), equals signs (=), English commas (,), Chinese commas (，), and Chinese periods (。) are allowed
- Up to 255 characters

MigrationJobName.description_en:
Task name
- Start with a letter or Chinese character
- Only Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), hyphens (-), and periods (.) are allowed
- Must be 1–128 characters long

TransitRouterRouteEntryNextHopId.description_en:
Next hop ID of the route entry.

* You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterVpcAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterVpcAttachments) API to obtain the ID of a VPC-type network instance connection.
* You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterVpnAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterVpnAttachments) API to obtain the ID of a VPN-type network instance connection.
* You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterDirectConnectGatewayAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterDirectConnectGatewayAttachments) API to obtain the ID of a Direct Connect Gateway-type network instance connection.
* You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterPeerAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterPeerAttachments) API to obtain the ID of a cross-region connection.

TransitRouterRouteEntryNextHopType.description_en:
Next hop type of the route entry. Valid values:

* Attachment: Network instance. Traffic matching this route entry will be forwarded to the specified network instance.
* BlackHole: Black hole. Traffic matching this route entry will be dropped.

TransitRouterRouteTableId.description_en: The ID of the route table associated with the transit router instance. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables) API to get the TR route table ID.

ActionResult.description_en:
Policy action of a routing policy entry. Possible values:

* Permit: Allow. Allows routes matching this routing policy entry to pass.
* Deny: Prevents routes matching this routing policy entry from passing.

ApplyAsPathValues.N.description_en:
Route AsPath set for the route policy entry. Value range: 1–4294967295.

* N: Indicates the sequence number of the route attribute, ranging from 1 to 10.
* Use & to separate multiple route attributes.

This parameter takes effect when `ActionResult` is set to "Permit".

AsPathOperateMode.description_en:
AsPath setting method for routing policy entries. The available values are:

* Additive: Appends an AsPath. Adds the specified AsPath to the beginning of the AsPath of permitted routes.
* Replace: Replaces the AsPath. Uses the specified AsPath to replace the AsPath of permitted routes.

This parameter takes effect only when `ActionResult` is set to "Permit".

* If this parameter is not specified, idempotency verification is not performed.

* Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Can include letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space ( ), equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。).

DestinationResourceIds.N.description_en:

* You can call the [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) API to obtain the ID of a VPC instance.
* You can call the [DescribeDirectConnectGateways](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/directconnect/DescribeDirectConnectGateways) API to obtain the ID of a Direct Connect Gateway instance.
* You can call the [DescribeTransitRouters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouters) API to obtain the ID of a cross-region TR instance.

* N: Indicates the sequence number of the destination instance ID, with a value range of 1–10. Use & to separate multiple destination instance IDs.
* After a value is provided for the parameter `DestinationResourceIds.N`, this parameter is required.
* When the routing policy direction is set to "In", this field must not be specified.

DestinationResourceTypes.N.description_en:
Destination instance type for the route policy entry. The values are as follows:

* You can call the [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) API to obtain the ID of a VPC instance.
* You can call the [DescribeDirectConnectGateways](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/directconnect/DescribeDirectConnectGateways) API to obtain the ID of a Direct Connect Gateway instance.
* You can call the [DescribeTransitRouters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouters) API to obtain the ID of a cross-region TR instance.

* N: Indicates the sequence number of the source instance ID, ranging from 1 to 10. Use & to separate multiple source instance IDs.
* After specifying the value for the parameter `SourceResourceTypes.N`, this parameter becomes required.

IpPrefixMatchMode.description_en:
Route prefix matching modes

* Include: Fuzzy matching. A match is successful if the route prefix in the matching condition includes the route prefix of the route being matched. For example, a policy entry with the route prefix 10.10.0.0/16 can match a route whose target subnet is 10.10.1.0/24 using fuzzy matching.
* Complete (default): Exact matching. A match is successful only if the route prefix in the matching condition is identical to the route prefix of the route being matched. For example, a policy entry with the route prefix 10.10.0.0/16 can only match a route whose target subnet is 10.10.0.0/16 exactly.

IpPrefixes.N.description_en:
Route prefix for the route policy entry. Supports IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR blocks.

* N: Indicates the sequence number of the route prefix, ranging from 1 to 200. Use & to separate multiple route prefixes.
* If this parameter is not provided or no value is specified, the default is an empty string.

The IPv6 feature for transit routers is currently in beta testing. To use this feature, please contact your account manager.

PrefixListId.description_en:
Prefix list ID associated with the route policy entry.
The transit router's support for VPC prefix lists is currently in beta testing. To use this feature, please contact your account manager.

Priority.description_en: Priority of the routing policy entry. Default is blank. Valid range: 1 to 10,000. Lower numbers have higher priority. Routing policy entries within the same policy cannot have duplicate priorities.

SourceResourceIds.N.description_en:

* You can call the [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) API to obtain the ID of a VPC instance.
* You can call the [DescribeDirectConnectGateways](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/directconnect/DescribeDirectConnectGateways) API to obtain the ID of a Direct Connect Gateway instance.
* You can call the [DescribeTransitRouters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouters) API to obtain the ID of a cross-region TR instance.

* N: Indicates the sequence number of the source instance ID, with a value range of 1–10. Use & to separate multiple source instance IDs.
* After a value is provided for the parameter `SourceResourceTypes.N`, this parameter is required.

SourceResourceTypes.N.description_en:

* VPC: Virtual Private Cloud
* DirectConnectGateway: Direct Connect Gateway
* TransitRouter: Cross-region TR

* N: Indicates the sequence number of the source instance type. You can specify up to 10 types in a single call. Use & to separate multiple source instance types.
* If this parameter is not specified or no value is provided, the default is an empty string.

TransitRouterMulticastDomainId.description_en: Multicast domain ID. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterMulticastDomains](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterMulticastDomains) API to get the multicast domain ID.

TransitRouterRouteTableId.description_en: ID of the route table associated with the transit router instance. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables) API to get the TR route table ID.

MaxResults.description_en: Number of items per query. Default is 10, maximum is 100.

NextToken.description_en: Pagination token, used to mark the position for paginated queries. No need to set this for the first call. For subsequent queries, use the NextToken value returned from the previous API call.

ResourceIds.N.description_en:
Resource ID.
- N: Indicates the sequence number of the resource ID, range is 1–50.
- Separate multiple resource IDs with &.

- You can call the [DescribeTransitRouters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouters) API to obtain the ID of resources of type "transitrouter".
- You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables) API to obtain the ID of resources of type "transitrouterroutetable".
- Depending on the resource type to be tagged, you can call [DescribeTransitRouterVpcAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterVpcAttachments), [DescribeTransitRouterVpnAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterVpnAttachments), [DescribeTransitRouterDirectConnectGatewayAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterDirectConnectGatewayAttachments), or [DescribeTransitRouterPeerAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterPeerAttachments) to obtain the ID of resources of type "transitrouterattachment".
- You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterBandwidthPackages](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterBandwidthPackages) API to obtain the ID of resources of type "transitrouterbandwidthpackage".

ResourceType.description_en:
Resource type. Valid values:
- transitrouter: Transit router instance.
- transitrouterroutetable: TR route table.
- transitrouterattachment: Instance attachment, including VPC, VPN, Direct Connect Gateway network instance attachments, and cross-region attachments.
- transitrouterbandwidthpackage: Transit router bandwidth package.

TagFilters.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key specified when querying resources by tag
- N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag key, with a value range of 1–10. Use & to separate multiple tag keys
- When multiple tag keys are specified, it means querying resources that contain all specified tag keys

TagFilters.N.Values.N.description_en:
Tag value for resource tags.
- The first N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag key, range is 1–10.
- The second N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag value, range is 1–3. Multiple tag values under the same tag key are logically "OR", meaning resources with any of the tag values under the same tag key will be queried.
- Separate multiple tag values with &.

- If this parameter is provided, TagFilters.N.Key must be set first.
- If this parameter is empty, it queries resources where the specified tag key has an empty tag value.

TagType.description_en:
Tag type. Valid values:
- custom: User tag.
- system: System tag.
- This parameter can be empty; in this case, all tag types are queried.

BillingOwnerType.description_en:
Billing entity for network instance connections

* `TransitRouterOwner`: The account that owns the transit router instance is responsible for the fees generated by the network instance connection
* `ResourceOwner`: The account that owns the network instance is responsible for the fees generated by the network instance connection

* Length must be between 0 and 255 characters
* If this parameter is not changed, the original configuration remains unchanged
Description.example_en: This transit router is used for testing.

TransitRouterMulticastDomainName.description_en:

Bandwidth.description_en:
Bandwidth for cross-region connections, measured in Mbps

BandwidthType.description_en:
Bandwidth allocation method for cross-region connections.

* BandwidthPackage: Allocated from bandwidth package
* CloudDataTransfer: Billed by traffic through Cloud Data Transfer Service

Description.description_en:
Description for the cross-region connection.

* Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Can include letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space ( ), equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。)

Description.example_en: Use this peer attachment for testing.

LineOperator.description_en:
Carrier for the cross-border bandwidth package route. This parameter is required for cross-border connectivity.

* ChinaUnicom: China Unicom
* ChinaTelecom: China Telecom

TransitRouterAttachmentName.description_en:

TransitRouterBandwidthPackageId.description_en: Transit router bandwidth package ID. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterBandwidthPackages](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterBandwidthPackages) API to get the transit router bandwidth package ID. If you provide this parameter, you must also provide the Bandwidth parameter; if you do not provide this parameter, Bandwidth is not required.

Description.description_en:
Description of the Transit Router route entry.

* Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Can contain letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space ( ), equal sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。)
* Length limit: 0–255 characters
* If this parameter is not specified or no value is provided, the default is an empty string
Description.example_en: This transit router is used for testing.

TransitRouterRouteEntryId.description_en: Transit Router route entry ID. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterRouteEntries](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterRouteEntries) API to get the Transit Router route entry ID.

TransitRouterRouteEntryName.description_en:
Name of the Transit Router route entry.

* Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Can contain letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: period (.), underscore (_), and hyphen (-)
* Length limit: 1–128 characters
* If this parameter is not specified or no value is provided, the default is the Transit Router route entry ID

Direction.description_en:
Direction of routing policy. Possible values:
- In: Receive direction. The transit router only receives routes that match the routing policy when learning routes from a network instance.
- Out: Send direction. The transit router only sends routes that match the routing policy when synchronizing routes to a network instance.

TransitRouterRoutePolicyTableId.description_en: Routing policy ID. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterRoutePolicyTables](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterRoutePolicyTables) API to get the routing policy ID.

TransitRouterRouteTableId.description_en: Transit router route table ID. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables) API to get the transit router route table ID.

ActionResult.description_en:
Routing policy entry actions. Available options:
- Permit: Allow routes that match this policy entry
- Deny: Block routes that match this policy entry

ApplyAsPathValues.N.description_en:
The route AsPath set for the routing policy entry. Value range: 1–4294967295
- N: Indicates the sequence number of the route attribute. Value range: 1–10
- Use & to separate multiple route attributes

This parameter takes effect only when ActionResult is set to "Permit"

AsPathOperateMode.description_en:
AsPath setting method for routing policy entries. Available options:
- Additive: Prepends the specified AsPath to the beginning of the permitted route's AsPath
- Replace: Replaces the permitted route's AsPath with the specified AsPath

This parameter takes effect only when ActionResult is set to Permit

Description.description_en:
Description for the routing policy entry
- Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character and can include letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space ( ), equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。)
- Length can be from 0 to 255 characters
- If you do not provide a value for this parameter, it defaults to an empty string
Description.example_en: This transit router is used for testing.

DestinationResourceIds.N.description_en:
Destination instance ID for the routing policy entry.
- You can call the [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) API to get the ID of a VPC instance.
- You can call the [DescribeDirectConnectGateways](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/directconnect/DescribeDirectConnectGateways) API to get the ID of a direct connect gateway instance.
- You can call the [DescribeTransitRouters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouters) API to get the ID of a cross-region transit router (TR) instance.

- N: Indicates the sequence number of the destination instance type, with a value range of 1–10. Use & to separate multiple destination instance types.
- When the routing policy direction is "In", this field cannot be specified.

DestinationResourceTypes.N.description_en:
Destination instance type for routing policy entries. Possible values:
- VPC: Virtual Private Cloud
- DirectConnectGateway: Direct Connect Gateway
- TransitRouter: Cross-region Transit Router

IpPrefixMatchMode.description_en:
Route Prefix Matching Modes
- Include: Contains match. The route prefix in the matching condition contains the route prefix of the route being matched, resulting in a successful match. For example, a policy entry with the route prefix 10.10.0.0/16 can loosely match a route with the target prefix 10.10.1.0/24.
- Complete: Exact match. The route prefix in the matching condition must be identical to the route prefix of the route being matched for a successful match. For example, a policy entry with the route prefix 10.10.0.0/16 can only exactly match a route with the target prefix 10.10.0.0/16.

IpPrefixes.N.description_en:
Route prefix for the routing policy entry
- Supports IPv4 and IPv6 network segments
- N indicates the sequence number of the route prefix, from 1 to 10. Use & to separate multiple route prefixes
- If you do not provide this parameter or leave it blank, the default is an empty string

PrefixListId.description_en: The IP prefix list ID associated with the route policy entry, used to specify a set of IP address prefixes as matching criteria.

Priority.description_en: Priority of the routing policy entry is empty by default. Valid range: 1 to 10,000. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Routing policy entries within the same policy cannot have duplicate priorities.

SourceResourceIds.N.description_en:
Source instance ID for the routing policy entry
- You can call the [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) API to get the ID of a private network instance
- You can call the [DescribeDirectConnectGateways](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/directconnect/DescribeDirectConnectGateways) API to get the ID of a Direct Connect Gateway instance
- You can call the [DescribeTransitRouters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouters) API to get the ID of a cross-region Transit Router (TR) instance

- N indicates the sequence number of the source instance ID, with a value range of 1–10. Use & to separate multiple source instance IDs
- After specifying a value for the SourceResourceTypes.N parameter, this parameter becomes required

SourceResourceTypes.N.description_en:
Source instance type for routing policy entries. Options:
- VPC: Virtual Private Cloud
- DirectConnectGateway: Direct Connect Gateway
- TransitRouter: Cross-region Transit Router

TransitRouterRoutePolicyEntryId.description_en: Route policy entry ID. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterRoutePolicyEntries](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterRoutePolicyEntries) API to get the route policy entry ID.

Description.description_en:
Description of the routing policy
- Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. It may include letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: English comma (,), English period (.), underscore (_), space, equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。)
- The length must be between 0 and 255 characters
- If this parameter is not provided or no value is provided, the default is an empty string

TransitRouterRoutePolicyTableName.description_en:
Routing policy name
- Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters are allowed: period (.), underscore (_), and hyphen (-)
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters

- Call the [DescribeTransitRouterVpnAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterVpnAttachments) API to get the ID of a VPN network instance connection
- Call the [DescribeTransitRouterDirectConnectGatewayAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterDirectConnectGatewayAttachments) API to get the ID of a Direct Connect Gateway network instance connection
- Call the [DescribeTransitRouterPeerAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterPeerAttachments) API to get the ID of a cross-region connection

TransitRouterRouteTableId.description_en: ID of the route table associated with the transit router instance. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables) API to get the transit router route table ID.

Description.description_en:
Description for the TR routing table
- Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Can include letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space ( ), equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。)
- Length must be between 0 and 255 characters
- If this parameter is not provided or left empty, the current configuration remains unchanged

TransitRouterRouteTableId.description_en: Route table ID associated with the transit router instance. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables) API to obtain the transit router route table ID.

TransitRouterRouteTableName.description_en:
Name of the TR routing table

TransitRouterAttachmentId.description_en:

TransitRouterTrafficQosMarkingPolicyId.description_en: Traffic QoS marking policy ID. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterTrafficQosMarkingPolicies](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterTrafficQosMarkingPolicies) API to obtain the traffic QoS marking policy ID.

Description.description_en:
Description for the flow tag policy.

- Length must be between 0 and 255 characters.

TransitRouterTrafficQosMarkingPolicyId.description_en: Traffic marking policy ID. Call the [DescribeTransitRouterTrafficQosMarkingPolicies](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterTrafficQosMarkingPolicies) API to get the traffic marking policy ID

TransitRouterTrafficQosMarkingPolicyName.description_en:
Flow tag policy name.

- If this parameter is not provided or no value is provided, the flow tag policy ID is used by default.

BandwidthPercent.description_en: The bandwidth percentage of the traffic queue. Value range: 0–100.

Description.description_en:
Queue description

* Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Can contain letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: English comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space ( ), equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。)

* If this parameter is not provided or no value is passed, the default is an empty string

TransitRouterTrafficQosQueueEntryId.description_en: ID of the transit router traffic QoS queue entry.

TransitRouterTrafficQosQueueEntryName.description_en:
Queue name

* Length limit: 1–128 characters
* If this parameter is not provided or no value is passed, the default is an empty string

TransitRouterAttachmentId.description_en:
Transit Router connection ID

TransitRouterTrafficQosQueuePolicyId.description_en: Traffic queue policy ID. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterTrafficQosQueuePolicies](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterTrafficQosQueuePolicies) API to obtain the traffic queue policy ID.

Description.description_en:
Description for the flow queue policy
- Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Allowed characters include letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space, equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。)
