TransitRouterTrafficQosQueuePolicyName.description_en:
Stream queue policy name
- Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Can include letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: period (.), underscore (_), and hyphen (-)
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
- If this parameter is not provided or no value is provided, the stream queue policy ID is used by default

ApplianceModeEnabled.description_en:
Whether to enable path consistency mode. Please enter the following enumerated values exactly as shown, including case. Do not use any other values.

* true: Yes. When enabled, TR forwards traffic to this VPC connection by selecting the same availability zone endpoint for both request and response traffic.
* false: No.

The path consistency feature for Transit Router is currently in invite-only testing. To use this feature, please contact your account manager.

AttachPoints.N.SubnetId.description_en:
Subnet ID of the network instance connection endpoint. You can call the [DescribeSubnets](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSubnets) API to obtain the subnet ID.

* N: Indicates the sequence number of the subnet ID, ranging from 1 to 100.
* Separate multiple subnet IDs with &.

AttachPoints.N.ZoneId.description_en:
ID of the availability zone to which the subnet belongs.

* N: Indicates the sequence number of the availability zone ID, ranging from 1 to 100.
* Separate multiple availability zone IDs with &.

AutoPublishRouteEnabled.description_en:
Whether to automatically synchronize TR routes to the network instance route table. Please enter the following enumerated values exactly as shown, including case. Do not use any other values.

* true: Yes. The system will automatically synchronize route entries from the TR route table associated with this network instance connection to the network instance's route table.
      The system will only automatically synchronize TR routes to the network instance's route table if this parameter is set to true and there are route entries in the TR route table associated with the network instance connection.
   
* false (default): No.

Description.description_en:
Description for the network instance connection.

* Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Can include letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: English comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space ( ), equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。)
* Length must be between 0 and 255 characters
* If you do not change the value of this parameter, the original configuration remains unchanged

Ipv6Enabled.description_en:
Whether to enable IPv6. Please enter the following enumerated values exactly as shown, including case. Do not use any other values.

* true: Yes.
* false: No.

The IPv6 feature for Transit Router is currently in invite-only testing. To use this feature, please contact your account manager.

TransitRouterAttachmentId.description_en: Network instance connection ID. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterVpcAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterVpcAttachments) API to get the ID of a VPC-type network instance connection.

TransitRouterAttachmentName.description_en:
Name of the network instance connection.

* Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Can contain letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: period (.), underscore (_), and hyphen (-).
* Length must be between 1 and 128 characters.
* If you do not change this parameter, the original configuration remains unchanged.

Description.description_en:
Description of the network instance connection

* Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Can include letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space ( ), equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。).
* Length limit: 0–255 characters.
* If you do not change this parameter value, the original configuration remains unchanged.

HealthCheckRevokeRouteEnabled.description_en:
Whether to enable the health check route convergence feature

* true: Yes. Takes effect only when the IPsec connection has health check enabled, and only supports converging static routes. BGP route convergence is not supported.
* false: No.

TransitRouterAttachmentId.description_en: Network instance connection ID. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterVpnAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterVpnAttachments) API to obtain the ID of a VPN-type network instance connection.

TransitRouterAttachmentName.description_en:
Name of the network instance connection

* Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Can include letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: period (.), underscore (_), and hyphen (-).
* Length limit: 1–128 characters.
* If you do not change this parameter value, the original configuration remains unchanged.

TransitRouterId.description_en: Transit router instance ID. You can call the [DescribeTransitRouters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouters) API to get the transit router instance ID.

TransitRouterAttachmentId.description_en: ID for cross-region connection

Period.description_en:
Purchase duration for the transit router bandwidth package. Default value is 1. Valid values are:
- If PeriodUnit is 'Month', valid values are 1–9, 12, 24, and 36
- If PeriodUnit is 'Year', valid values are 1–3

PeriodUnit.description_en:
Billing cycle for transit router bandwidth package. Available options:
- Month (default): Billed monthly
- Year: Billed yearly

RemainRenewTimes.description_en:
Number of auto-renewals
Values: -1 or 1–100. Default is -1, which means unlimited auto-renewals
Effective when `RenewType` is set to Auto

RenewPeriod.description_en:
Duration of each automatic renewal, in months
Valid values: 1–3, 6, and 12; default is 1
Effective when `RenewType` is set to Auto

RenewType.description_en:
Renewal types for transit router bandwidth packages. Available options:
- Manual: Renew manually
- Auto: Renew automatically
- NoRenew: Do not renew

TransitRouterBandwidthPackageId.description_en: Transit router bandwidth package ID. Call the [DescribeTransitRouterBandwidthPackages](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterBandwidthPackages) API to query the transit router bandwidth package ID.

ResourceIds.N.description_en:
Resource ID.
- N indicates the sequence number of the resource ID, range: 1–50
- Use & to separate multiple resource IDs

- You can call the [DescribeTransitRouters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouters) API to get the ID of a 'transitrouter' resource
- You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables) API to get the ID of a 'transitrouterroutetable' resource
- Depending on the resource type to be tagged, you can call [DescribeTransitRouterVpcAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterVpcAttachments), [DescribeTransitRouterVpnAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterVpnAttachments), [DescribeTransitRouterDirectConnectGatewayAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterDirectConnectGatewayAttachments), or [DescribeTransitRouterPeerAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterPeerAttachments) to get the ID of a 'transitrouterattachment' resource
- You can call [DescribeTransitRouterMulticastDomains](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterMulticastDomains) to get the ID of a 'transitroutermulticastdomain' resource
- You can call [DescribeTransitRouterBandwidthPackages](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterBandwidthPackages) API to get the ID of a 'transitrouterbandwidthpackage' resource

ResourceType.description_en:
Resource type. Possible values are as follows:
- transitrouter: Transit router instance
- transitrouterroutetable: TR route table
- transitrouterattachment: Instance attachment, including VPC, VPN, Direct Connect Gateway network instance attachments, and cross-region attachments
- transitroutermulticastdomain: TR multicast domain
- transitrouterbandwidthpackage: Transit router bandwidth package

Tags.N.Key.description_en:
User tag key.
- Length limit: 1–128 characters
- Case-sensitive; cannot start with any combination of 'volc:' or 'sys:' (case-insensitive)
- Cannot start or end with a space
- Can include characters from any language, numbers, spaces (), underscores (_), periods (.), colons (:), slashes (/), equals signs (=), plus signs (+), minus signs (-), and @

- Tag keys for the same resource cannot be duplicated. If the Tags.N.Key you pass is the same as an existing tag key, the newly added tag will overwrite the original tag
- If you do not pass this parameter or do not provide a value, it defaults to empty

Tags.N.Value.description_en:
User tag value.
- Length limit: 1–256 characters
- Case-sensitive; cannot start or end with a space
- Can include characters from any language, numbers, spaces (), underscores (_), periods (.), colons (:), slashes (/), equals signs (=), plus signs (+), minus signs (-), and @

If you pass this parameter, you must first pass Tags.N.Key

ResourceIds.N.description_en:
Resource ID
- N: Indicates the sequence number of the resource ID. The maximum number of IDs per request is 50
- Separate multiple resource IDs with &

- You can call the [DescribeTransitRouters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouters) API to get the ID of a 'transitrouter' resource
- You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterRouteTables) API to get the ID of a 'transitrouterroutetable' resource
- Depending on the type of resource you want to tag, you can call the [DescribeTransitRouterVpcAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterVpcAttachments) API, [DescribeTransitRouterVpnAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterVpnAttachments) API, [DescribeTransitRouterDirectConnectGatewayAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterDirectConnectGatewayAttachments) API, or [DescribeTransitRouterPeerAttachments](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterPeerAttachments) API to get the ID of a 'transitrouterattachment' resource
- You can call the [DescribeTransitRouterBandwidthPackages](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterBandwidthPackages) API to get the ID of a 'transitrouterbandwidthpackage' resource

ResourceType.description_en:
Resource types and their values:
- transitrouter: Transit router instance
- transitrouterroutetable: Transit router route table
- transitrouterattachment: Instance attachment, including VPC, VPN, dedicated gateway network instance attachments, and cross-region attachments
- transitrouterbandwidthpackage: Transit router bandwidth package

TagKeys.N.description_en:
Tag key of the user label to be deleted. Cannot start or end with a space
- N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag key, ranging from 1 to 20
- Use & to separate multiple tag keys

If the specified Tags.N.Key does not exist or is already unbound, the system returns success by default without an error

InstanceIds.description_en:
Instance IDs to bind tags to
- You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/NDB_for_MySQL/DescribeDBInstances) API to query basic information for all instances in the target region, including instance IDs.
- You can specify up to 20 instance IDs at a time; each instance can have up to 50 tags.

Tags.description_en:
Array object of tag keys and tag values to bind
- You can bind up to 20 tag key-value pairs in a single request. Each instance supports up to 50 tags
- Tag keys and values must follow the configuration rules. For details, see [Tag configuration rules](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/NDB_for_MySQL/Tag_overview#标签设置规则)

InstanceIds.description_en:
Instance ID. Use commas (,) to separate multiple instance IDs.
You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/NDB_for_MySQL/DescribeDBInstances) API to query instance IDs.

ScheduleType.description_en:
Execution Mode, values:
- `Immediate`: Execute immediately (default)
- `MaintainTime`: Execute during maintainable time period

TemplateId.description_en:
Parameter template ID.
You can call the [DescribeParameterTemplates](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/NDB_for_MySQL/DescribeParameterTemplates) API to query the parameter template ID.

AllowListIds.description_en:
Allowlist ID to be bound to the instance.
* You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/NDB_for_MySQL/DescribeAllowLists) API to query the list of all allowlists in the specified region, including allowlist IDs.
* You cannot pass multiple instance IDs and allowlist IDs at the same time. You can only bind multiple instances to the same allowlist at once, or bind one instance to multiple allowlists at once.

InstanceIds.description_en:
Instance ID to be bound to the allowlist.
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/NDB_for_MySQL/DescribeDBInstances) API to query basic information for all instances in the target region, including instance IDs.
* You cannot pass multiple instance IDs and allowlist IDs at the same time. You can only bind multiple instances to the same allowlist at once, or bind one instance to multiple allowlists at once.

EventId.description_en:
Event IDs. Separate multiple event IDs with commas (,).
* You can cancel up to 100 events in a batch.
* You can call the [DescribeScheduleEvents](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/NDB_for_MySQL/DescribeScheduleEvents) API to query scheduled events pending execution under your current account.

InstanceIds.description_en:
The instance IDs to which the events to be canceled belong. Separate multiple instance IDs with commas (,).
You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/NDB_for_MySQL/DescribeDBInstances) API to query basic information about all instances in the target region, including instance IDs.

ClusterName.description_en:
Instance ID.
You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/NDB_for_MySQL/DescribeDBInstances) API to query the instance ID.

TargetNode.description_en:
ID of the read-only node to be switched to the primary node.
You must provide the ID of the read-only node, that is, the value of `NodeType` must be `ReadOnly`. You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/NDB_for_MySQL/DescribeDBInstanceDetail) API to query detailed information about the specified instance.

BackupMethod.description_en: Backup method. Only physical backup is supported; set to `Physical`

BackupType.description_en: Backup type: Currently, only full backup is supported; set to `Full`

Instance ID.
You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/NDB_for_MySQL/DescribeDBInstances) API to query the instance ID.

AccountDesc.description_en: Account description information, 0–256 characters. Can include numbers, Chinese characters, English letters, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)

AccountName.description_en:
Database account name. The account name must meet the following requirements:

* The name must be unique and between 2 and 32 characters in length.
* It can contain letters, numbers, hyphens (-), and underscores (_).
* It must start with a letter and end with a letter or number.
* The name cannot contain certain prohibited words. For details, see [Prohibited Keywords](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/NDB_for_MySQL/List_of_forbidden_keywords). You also cannot use certain reserved words, such as root, admin, etc.

AccountPassword.description_en:
Password for the database account. The account password must meet the following requirements:

* It can only contain uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and the following special characters: `~!@#$%^&*_-+=`|\(){}[]:;'<>,.?/`.
* The length must be between 8 and 32 characters.
* It must contain at least three of the following: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, or special characters.

AccountPrivileges.description_en:
Database privilege information.
* When `AccountType` is set to `Super`, you do not need to provide this parameter. The high-privilege account automatically has all privileges for all databases under this instance.
* When `AccountType` is set to `Normal`, it is recommended to provide this parameter to grant specific privileges for specified databases to the normal account. If not set, the account will not have any privileges for any database.

AccountType.description_en:
Database account type. Values:

* `Super`: High-privilege account. Only one high-privilege account can be created per instance, and it has all privileges for all databases under the instance. It can manage all normal accounts and databases.
* `Normal`: Multiple normal accounts can be created per instance. You need to manually grant specific privileges for specified databases to normal accounts.

InstanceId.description_en:
Instance ID.
You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/NDB_for_MySQL/DescribeDBInstances) API to query the instance ID.

EipId.description_en:
EIP ID to be bound to the instance.
You can call the [DescribeEipAddresses](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/eip/DescribeEipAddressAttributes) API to query details of created EIPs, including the EIP ID.

EndpointId.description_en:

DBDesc.description_en: Database description. Length: 0–256 characters. You can use numbers, Chinese characters, English letters, underscores (_) and hyphens (-)

DBName.description_en:
Database name. Naming rules:

* The database name must be unique within the current instance.
* Length: 2–64 characters. Must start with a letter and end with a letter or number.
* Can contain letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-).
* Database names cannot use certain reserved words. For details, see [Disabled Keywords](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/NDB_for_MySQL/List_of_forbidden_keywords).

TemplateParameters.description_en: The parameter template contains information about parameters and parameter values.

SnapshotId.description_en:
Snapshot ID for forking a new instance from a snapshot (optional)
Once set, this request switches to the "Fork from snapshot" mode:
  - Fields such as sandbox image, Port, Command, TOS/NAS/EBS/EmptyDir, Metadata, RoleChainTrn, RoleTrn
    are all sourced from the snapshot itself; corresponding fields in the request body will be ignored
  - Timeout / TimeoutUnit / SessionId / Async / CpuMilli / MemoryMB / RequestTimeout / MaxConcurrency
    can be overridden by this request; CpuMilli / MemoryMB must be >= the specs recorded in the snapshot, otherwise InvalidParameter is returned
  - Envs support key-based merge and override: environment variables with the same name in the request override snapshot values, other variables from the snapshot are retained
  - If Sidecars are provided, they completely replace the sidecars in the snapshot (an empty list means no sidecar is used); if not provided, the snapshot configuration is used
  - InstanceTosMountConfig supports adding mounts during fork:
      * If the snapshot itself does not have TOS mounts: the configuration in the request will be used as the mount point for the forked instance
      * If the snapshot already includes TOS mounts: mount points in the request will be appended after the snapshot mount points
        After merging, all LocalMountPath values must be globally unique (no conflicts between TOS and EBS)
        If there is a conflict, InvalidParameter is returned; the request cannot override original mount points from the snapshot

The cluster must be in the `{Running,[Ok]}` or `{Updating,[Progressing]}` state. You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to get the current status of the cluster.

Name.description_en:
Node pool name

* The node pool name must be unique within the same cluster
* Supports uppercase and lowercase English letters, Chinese characters, numbers, and hyphens (-); length must be between 2 and 64 characters

Do not use the reserved default node pool name: `vke-default-nodepool`

NodeConfig.description_en: ECS Instance Configuration in the Node Pool

Tags.description_en:
Custom resource tags let you classify, search, and aggregate node pools with similar characteristics from different dimensions, enabling flexible node pool management.

* Each Key in Tags must be unique
* If a resource already has the same Tags.Key, binding the same Tags.Key again will not cause an error; the Tags.Value will be updated to the latest value
* A single resource can have up to 50 Tags
* Spaces are not allowed at the beginning or end of Key or Value in Tags

AdditionalContainerStorageEnabled.description_en:
Select and configure a node's data disk, format and mount it as the storage directory for container images and logs. Values:

* **false** (default): Disabled
   * Default node pool: Data disk will not be mounted.
   * Custom node pool: Mounting uses the node pool's data disk configuration. The ECS instance data disk added to the node pool must include the data disk specified for mounting by the target node pool (including local disks), and the disk type and size must match exactly.
* **true**: Enabled. You must also configure the **ContainerStoragePath** parameter. The node will mount according to the configuration in the **ContainerStoragePath** parameter, ignoring the node pool's data disk configuration. There are no special requirements for the ECS instance data disk added to the node pool.

ClientToken.description_en: String used to ensure request idempotency. The caller provides this string and must ensure it is unique for each request. ClientToken is case-sensitive and cannot exceed 64 ASCII characters.

ClusterId.description_en:
Cluster ID.
You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to get the cluster ID.
The cluster must be in the `{Running,[*]}` or `{Updating,[Progressing]}` state. You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to check the current cluster status.

ContainerStoragePath.description_en:
Use this data disk device to mount the `/var/lib/containerd` directory for container and image storage.
This parameter is only valid when `AdditionalContainerStorageEnabled=true` and must not be empty.
The following conditions must be met, otherwise initialization will fail:

* Only ECS instances with mounted data disks are supported.
* If you specify a data disk device name, ensure the device exists; otherwise, initialization will fail.
* If you specify a data disk partition or logical volume name, ensure the partition or logical volume exists and uses the ext4 file system.

* If you specify a data disk device, it will be automatically formatted and mounted directly. Please back up your data in advance.
* If you specify a data disk partition or logical volume name, formatting is not required.

GpuDriverConfig.description_en:
Node GPU driver configuration. This configuration takes precedence over the `GpuDriverVersion` field.
* This parameter applies to both the default node pool and custom node pools.
* If added to a custom node pool without configuring this parameter, nodes inherit the `GpuDriverConfig` configuration from the custom node pool.

GpuDriverVersion.description_en:
**[This parameter is deprecated. Please use GpuDriverConfig instead]** Specifies the GPU driver version installed on the node.
You can call the [ListSupportedGpuDriverVersions](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListSupportedGpuDriverVersions) API to obtain the list of GPU driver versions supported by the image.

ImageId.description_en:
The image ID used by the ECS instance corresponding to the node.
Different image types have different image IDs. For details, see [Public Images Supported by Container Service](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/Overview-of-operating-system-images#%E5%AE%B9%E5%99%A8%E6%9C%8D%E5%8A%A1%E6%94%AF%E6%8C%81%E7%9A%84%E5%85%AC%E5%85%B1%E9%95%9C%E5%83%8F).
If this parameter is not provided, Container Service will assign the default **veLinux-VKE** image ID according to the ECS instance type you selected.

InitializeScript.description_en:
Script executed after creating the ECS node and completing Kubernetes component deployment. Supports Shell format. The length after Base64 encoding must not exceed 1 KB.

* If left empty, the node inherits the default node pool initialization script `NodeConfig.InitializeScript`.
* If you provide a custom script, the custom script will be used and the default node pool initialization script will be ignored.

After Base64 encoding, the length must not exceed 8 KB. If both **InitializeScript** and **PreScript** are provided, the total length of both parameters must not exceed 8 KB.

InstanceIds.description_en:
ECS instance IDs to add to the cluster. You can specify up to 100 ECS instance IDs in a single request.
Call the [DescribeInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeInstances) API to obtain ECS instance IDs. The ECS instances must meet the following requirements:

* Located in the same VPC as the cluster
* Not used by another cluster
* Instance status must be **Running** (`Running`)
* The number of nodes added cannot exceed the cluster's maximum supported node count
* Do not add the same ECS instance more than once

If you are adding ECS instances to a custom node pool, note the following:

* If the node pool has **AffinityGroupConfig** enabled (invite-only), the number of ECS instance IDs entered here must be a multiple of the affinity group specification; otherwise, the addition will fail
* If the node pool does not have **AffinityGroupConfig** enabled (invite-only), specifying affinity group ECS instance IDs may cause unexpected behavior. We recommend not selecting affinity group ECS instances in node pools purchased without affinity group configuration

KeepContainerdDirectory.description_en:
Before mounting the data disk, should the `containerd` directory be cleaned? Options:

* **true**: Clean
* **false**: Do not clean

KeepInstanceName.description_en:
Whether to retain the original ECS instance name. Values:

* **false**: (default) Do not retain the original ECS instance name; Container Service will automatically assign a name.
* **true**: Retain the original ECS instance name.

KubernetesConfig.description_en:
Node Kubernetes-related configuration.

* If empty, the node inherits the default node pool's Kubernetes configuration `KubernetesConfig.Labels/Taints/Cordon`
* If you enter a custom configuration, the custom configuration will be used and the default node pool's Kubernetes configuration will be ignored

NamePrefix.description_en:
Node name prefix. Lower priority than **KeepInstanceName**. If set to an empty string, the node name prefix is not enabled.
Validation rules:

* Supports English letters, numbers, and hyphens (-); hyphens (-) cannot be used consecutively
* Must start with an English letter and end with an English letter or number
* Length must be 2–51 characters

NodePoolId.description_en:
Node pool ID

* If no parameter value is provided: existing ECS instances will be added to the default node pool.
* If a parameter value is provided: existing ECS instances will be added to a custom node pool. You can call the [ListNodePools](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListNodePools) API to obtain the target custom node pool ID.

If you enter a **custom node pool ID** here, the nodes to be added will use the Kubernetes configuration and node settings from the custom node pool (including ECS instance tags, labels, taints, node blocking configuration, project, node name prefix, etc). Therefore, the **InitializeScript**, **KubernetesConfig**, and **ImageId** parameter settings will be ignored. These parameters are only valid when adding existing nodes to the default node pool.

PreScript.description_en:
[Invite Test · Apply for Trial](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/How-do-I-apply-for-beta-features) Script executed before deploying the node. Enter a Shell script in Base64 encoding.
* If the parameter value is empty, the node to be added inherits the default node pool's pre-script configuration **NodeConfigRequest.PreScript**
* If you enter a custom script, the default node pool pre-script will be ignored and the script entered here will be used
* The length after Base64 encoding must not exceed 8 KB. If both **InitializeScript** and **PreScript** are provided, the total length of both parameters must not exceed 8 KB

Roles.description_en:
Node role. Values:

* Master: master node
* Etcd: etcd node
* Worker: worker node

SkipReplaceSystem.description_en:
Skip system reset when adding existing nodes:

* **true**: Skip system reset; the operating system of the ECS instance for the existing node will not be reset
* **false** (default): Do not skip system reset; the operating system of the ECS instance for the existing node will be reset

If you need to skip system reset (set to `true`), make sure:

* The ECS instance status is **RUNNING**. You can call [DescribeInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeInstances) to check the instance status
* The ECS instance has Cloud Assistant Agent installed and its status is **Running**. You can call [DescribeCloudAssistantStatus](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeCloudAssistantStatus) to check the Cloud Assistant Agent status

AdjustmentValue.description_en: Number of nodes to add during node pool elastic scaling. Must be an integer between 1 and 500.

ClientToken.description_en: A string used to ensure idempotency of requests. This string is provided by the caller and must be unique across different requests. ClientToken is case-sensitive and must not exceed 64 ASCII characters.

ClusterId.description_en:
Cluster ID.
You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to get the cluster ID.
The cluster must be in the `{Running,[Ok]}` or `{Updating,[Progressing]}` state. You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to get the current status of the cluster.

Enabled.description_en:
Whether to enable the scaling policy. Values:

* **true**: Enable
* **false**: (default) Disable

NodePoolId.description_en:
Node pool ID.
The node pool must be in the `{Running,[*]}` state. You can call the [ListNodePools](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListNodePools) API to get the current status of the node pool.

Type.description_en:
Type of scaling policy. Values:

* **Scheduled**: Scheduled task
* **Recurrence**: Recurring task

ClientToken.description_en: ClientToken

Description.description_en: Snapshot Description

CascadingDeleteResources.description_en:
Parameter deprecation notice:

* Only **existing users** can use this parameter. For how to determine if you are an existing user, see the [FAQ](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467)
* As this parameter will soon be deprecated, **existing users** can only use it within a specified period. Please complete the API migration as soon as possible and use the new **RetainResources** parameter. For migration instructions, see [OpenAPI Migration Guide for Cascading Deletion of Cluster Resources](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467)
* **New users** (those who enabled and started using VKE after December 18, 2023) should use the **RetainResources** parameter

Cascading deletion of resources associated with the component. Valid values:

* Leave empty: (default) Do not cascade delete associated resources
* **Crd**: Delete the component's CRD (Custom Resource Definition) resources synchronously. Resources from other external systems do not support cascading deletion, such as load balancers associated with Ingress, log projects (Project), and log topics (Topic) associated with log components

ClusterId.description_en:
ID of the cluster to which the component to be uninstalled belongs
You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to get the cluster ID
The cluster must be in `{Running,[Ok]}` or `{Updating, [Progressing]}` status. You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to get the current status of the cluster

Name.description_en:
Name of the component to be uninstalled
You can call the [ListAddons](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListAddons) API to get the component name
The component must **not be in** `{Creating, [Progressing]}`, `{Deleting, [Progressing]}`, or `{Failed, [ClusterNotRunning]}` status. You can call the [ListAddons](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListAddons) API to get the current status of the component

RetainResources.description_en:
* **Existing users** must complete the [API migration](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467) before using this parameter. For how to determine if you are an existing user, see the [FAQ](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467)
* **New users** (those who enabled and started using VKE after December 18, 2023) can use this parameter directly

Resources to retain when deleting the component. Valid values:

* Leave empty: (default) Delete all associated resources
      Resources from other external systems do not support cascading deletion, such as load balancers associated with Ingress, log projects (Project), and log topics (Topic) associated with log components
   
* **Crd**: Retain the component's CRD (Custom Resource Definition) resources when deleting the component

CascadingDeleteResources.description_en:
Parameter deprecation notice:

* Only **existing users** can use this parameter. For criteria to determine existing users, see [FAQ](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467).
* As this parameter will soon be discontinued, **existing users** can only use it within a specified timeframe. Please promptly update your interface and use the new **RetainResources** parameter. For interface update instructions, see [OpenAPI update instructions for cascading cluster resource deletion](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467).
* **New users** (those who activated and started using VKE after December 18, 2023) should use the **RetainResources** parameter.

Synchronously delete related resources in the specified cluster. Options:

* **DefaultNodePoolResource**: Synchronously delete ECS instances in the default node pool of the cluster.
   If the default node pool contains subscription ECS instances, this interface only removes the ECS instances from the cluster without deleting them. You can find these instances in the [ECS console](https://console.volcengine.com/ecs) or via the [ECS API](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Elastic-Compute-Service-API-overview) and perform follow-up actions as needed.
* **NodePoolResource**: Synchronously delete all custom node pools in the cluster, ECS instances in the node pools, and their associated elastic block storage.
   Does not include storage resources corresponding to persistent volumes (PV), such as EBS, NAS file storage, vePFS file storage, object storage (TOS), etc.
* **Clb**: Synchronously delete load balancers (CLB) created by the cluster.
* **Nat**: Synchronously delete NAT gateways created by the cluster.
* **All**: Synchronously delete all the above resource types in the cluster, except for
   subscription nodes in the cluster, storage resources corresponding to PVs, and Topics associated with log services.

During deletion, resources with deletion protection enabled cannot be deleted. Resources without deletion protection will be deleted. Adjust deletion protection settings as needed before calling the interface.

Force.description_en:
Force delete cluster, options:

* **false** (default): Disabled
* **true**: Enabled. When set to this value, clusters with deletion protection enabled (`DeleteProtection=true`) can also be forcibly deleted.

Id.description_en:
Cluster ID to be deleted.
You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to obtain the cluster ID.
The cluster to be deleted must be in one of the following states:

* `{Running,[*]}`
* `{Failed, [*]}`
* `{Stopped, [Ok, Balance]}`

You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to check the current status of the cluster.

RetainResources.description_en:
* **Existing users** must complete the [API upgrade](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467) before using this parameter. For how to determine existing users, see the [FAQ](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467).
* **New users** (those who activated and used VKE after December 18, 2023) can use this parameter directly.

When deleting a cluster, specify which resources within the cluster to retain:

* Leave blank (default): Deletes all resources created in association with the cluster, as well as non-subscription ECS instances added to the node pool.
* **DefaultNodePoolResource**: Retains ECS instances in the default node pool and their associated Elastic Block Storage, public IPs, and other resources.
* **NodePoolResource**: Retains ECS instances in all custom node pools and their associated Elastic Block Storage, public IPs, and other resources.
* **Clb**: Retains load balancer (CLB) instances created by Ingress and Service within the cluster.
* **Alb**: Retains application load balancer (ALB) instances created by Ingress and Service within the cluster.
* **Nat**: Retains NAT gateways created in association with the cluster.
* **SecurityGroup**: Retains security groups created in association with the cluster.
* **All**: Retains all resources created in association with the cluster.

If deletion protection is enabled for these resources, they cannot be deleted. Resources without deletion protection will be deleted. Adjust deletion protection settings as needed before calling the API.

ClusterId.description_en:
Cluster ID
You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to get the cluster ID.

The cluster must be in the `{Running,[Ok]}` or `{Updating,[Progressing]}` state. You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to check the current cluster status.

Ids.description_en:
Kubeconfig ID

On the [Container Service Console](https://console.volcengine.com/vke), go to the **Cluster** page and click the target cluster name. On the cluster's **Basic Information** page, select the **Connection Info** tab to get the Kubeconfig ID. You can also view the Kubeconfig ID saved after calling the [CreateKubeconfig](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/CreateKubeconfig) API.

CascadingDeleteResources.description_en:

Please complete the API upgrade and use the new **RetainResources** parameter as soon as possible. For upgrade instructions, see [OpenAPI upgrade instructions for cascading cluster resource deletion](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467).
* **New users** (those who activated and started using VKE after December 18, 2023) should use the **RetainResources** parameter.

Synchronously delete associated resources. Options:

* Leave blank (default): Do not delete associated resources.
* **Ecs**: Delete non-subscription ECS instances in the node pool.
   Subscription-based ECS instances are only removed from the node pool and are not deleted. You can find these instances in the [ECS Console](https://console.volcengine.com/ecs) or via the [ECS API](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Elastic-Compute-Service-API-overview) and perform follow-up actions as needed.

If deletion protection is enabled for these resources, they cannot be deleted. Resources without deletion protection will be deleted. Adjust deletion protection settings as needed before calling the API.

ClusterId.description_en:
Cluster ID where the node pool is located
You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to obtain the cluster ID
The cluster containing the node pool to be deleted must be in one of the following states:

* `{Running,[*]}`
* `{Updating, [Progressing]}`
* `{Stopped, [Balance]}`

You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to check the current status of the cluster

Id.description_en:
Node pool ID
You can call the [ListNodePools](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListNodePools) API to obtain the node pool ID
The node pool must be in one of the following states:

* `{Running,[*]}`
* `{Failed, [*]}`

You can call the [ListNodePools](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListNodePools) API to check the current status of the node pool

RetainResources.description_en:
* **Existing users** must complete the [API upgrade](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467) before using this parameter. For how to determine existing users, see the [FAQ](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467).
* **New users** (those who activated and started using VKE after December 18, 2023) can use this parameter directly.

When deleting a node pool, specify which related resources to retain:

* Leave blank (default): Delete all associated resources.
   If the node pool contains subscription-based ECS instances, this API only removes the ECS instances from the node pool and does not delete them. You can find these instances in the [ECS Console](https://console.volcengine.com/ecs) or via the [ECS API](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Elastic-Compute-Service-API-overview) and perform follow-up actions as needed.
* **Ecs**: Retain ECS instances in the node pool.

If deletion protection is enabled for these resources, they cannot be deleted. Resources without deletion protection will be deleted. Adjust deletion protection settings as needed before calling the API.

CascadingDeleteResources.description_en:
Parameter deprecation notice:

* Only **existing users** can use this parameter. For how to determine if you are an existing user, see [FAQ](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467).
* As this parameter will soon be deprecated, **existing users** can only use it within a specified period. Please complete the API update as soon as possible and use the new **RetainResources** parameter. For update instructions, see [OpenAPI update instructions for cascading deletion of cluster resources](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467).
* **New users** (who activated and started using VKE after December 18, 2023) should use the **RetainResources** parameter.

Synchronously delete resources associated with the specified nodes. Value options:

* Leave blank: (default) Do not delete associated resources
* **Ecs**: Delete pay-as-you-go cloud server (ECS) instances
   Subscription ECS instances are only removed from the cluster and will not be deleted. You can find these instances in the [Cloud Server Console](https://console.volcengine.com/ecs) or via the [Cloud Server API](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Elastic-Compute-Service-API-overview), and perform further actions as needed.

During deletion, resources with deletion protection enabled cannot be deleted; resources without deletion protection will be deleted. It is recommended to adjust deletion protection settings as needed before calling the API.

ClusterId.description_en:
Cluster ID
You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to get the cluster ID.
The cluster must be in one of the following states:

* `{Running,[*]}`
* `{Updating, [Progressing]}`
* `{Stopped, [Balance]}`

You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to get the current state of the cluster.

Drain.description_en: Drain the node before deletion; not performed by default

Ids.description_en:
Node ID list
You can call the [ListNodes](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListNodes) API to obtain node IDs. You can specify up to 100 node IDs per request.
* Nodes must be in one of the following states:
   * `{Running,[*]}`
   * `{Stopped, [*]}`
   * `{Failed, [InitilizeFailed, NotReady, ResourceCleanupFailed, Balance, Unknown]}`
   You can call the [ListNodes](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListNodes) API to check the current status of nodes.
* When decommissioning [Elastic Bare Metal](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/General-purpose-EBM) nodes, ECS will attempt a normal shutdown based on the running status. If a normal shutdown fails, a forced shutdown will be performed. For more information, see [StopInstance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/StopInstance).
* If the specified node pool has **AffinityGroupConfig** affinity group configuration (preview), you must ensure that after removing nodes from the pool, the remaining number of nodes is an integer multiple of the affinity group specification. You can also remove all nodes from the node pool.

NodePoolId.description_en:
Node pool ID
You can call the [ListNodePools](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListNodePools) API to get the node pool ID.
The node pool must be in one of the following states:

* `{Running,[*]}`
* `{Scaling,[Progressing]}`
* `{Failed, [ClusterNotRunning, ResourceCleanupFailed]}`

You can call the [ListNodePools](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListNodePools) API to get the current state of the node pool.

RetainResources.description_en:
* **Existing users** must complete the [API upgrade](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467) before using this parameter. For how to determine if you are an existing user, see the [FAQ](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6460/1182467).
* **New users** (those who activated and started using VKE after December 18, 2023) can use this parameter directly.

When deleting a node, specify which associated resources to retain:

* Leave blank (default): Delete all associated resources.
   If the node is a cloud server (ECS) instance with annual/monthly subscription, this API only removes the ECS instance from the node but does not delete it. You can find the instance in the [Cloud Server Console](https://console.volcengine.com/ecs) or via the [Cloud Server API](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Elastic-Compute-Service-API-overview) and perform further actions as needed.
* **Ecs**: Retain the ECS instance associated with the node.

During deletion, resources with deletion protection enabled cannot be deleted; resources without deletion protection will continue to be deleted. We recommend adjusting deletion protection settings as needed before calling the API.

ClusterId.description_en:

You can call the [ListClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/ListClusters) API to get the cluster ID.

DefaultDeleteAllResources.description_en:
Configure the global policy for cluster resource deletion OpenAPIs ([DeleteCluster](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/DeleteCluster), [DeleteNodePool](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/DeleteNodePool), [DeleteNodes](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/DeleteNodes), [DeleteAddon](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vke/DeleteAddon)). Change the default OpenAPI behavior to synchronously delete related resources to prevent resource remnants.

- **false**: Default value. When calling cluster resource deletion OpenAPIs, the legacy parameter **CascadingDeleteResources** is used. By default, this parameter retains all cluster-related resources and does not perform cascading deletion.
- **true**: When calling cluster resource deletion OpenAPIs, the new parameter **RetainResources** is used. By default, this parameter deletes all cluster-related resources to avoid unnecessary costs from leftover resources.

If you set this parameter to **true** and do not change it again within 30 days, the new parameter configuration policy will be considered accepted. Afterward, only the **RetainResources** parameter will be allowed in the above OpenAPI calls to specify which resources to retain during deletion.

Ipv6Address.N.description_en:

   * When the network interface is in the InUse state, the value range for N is limited by the instance type. For more details, see [Instance Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Introduction-to-instance-types).
* Separate multiple private IPv6 addresses with &.
* The specified private IPv6 addresses must be available private IPv6 addresses within the subnet to which the network interface belongs.

You must provide either the `Ipv6Address.N` or `Ipv6AddressCount` parameter, but not both.

You can call the [DescribeIpv6Gateways](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/IPv6/DescribeIpv6Gateways) API to query the IPv6 gateway ID.

Name.description_en:
Egress-only rule name

* Length limit: 1–128 characters
* Must start with a letter, Chinese character, or number. Can include period (.), underscore (_), and hyphen (-)
* If not specified, defaults to the egress-only rule ID

ClientToken.description_en:
Client token used to ensure request idempotency.

* This parameter is automatically generated by the client to ensure uniqueness for different requests, preventing repeated operations when the API call times out or there is a server internal error and the client retries multiple times.
* Only ASCII characters are supported, with a maximum length of 64 characters.
* If this parameter is not specified, idempotency is not checked.

Description.description_en:
Description of the IPv6 gateway instance.

* Length limit: 0–255 characters.
* If not specified, defaults to an empty string.
* Must start with a letter, Chinese character, or number. Can include English comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space ( ), equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。).

Name.description_en:
Name of the IPv6 gateway instance

* Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
* Must start with a letter, Chinese character, or number; can include periods (.), underscores (_), and hyphens (-)
* If left blank, the default is the IPv6 gateway ID

ProjectName.description_en: Name of the project to which the IPv6 gateway belongs. If not specified, it will be added to the default project.

Tags.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key for user tags.

* Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag key, range: 1–50.
* Separate multiple tag keys with &.
* Cannot start with `volc:` or `sys:`, in any case.
* Length range: 1–128 characters. Supports input of characters from any language, numbers, spaces ( ), underscores (_), periods (.), colons (:), slashes (/), equals signs (=), plus signs (+), hyphens (-), and @ (@).
* If the tag key starts or ends with a space, the system will automatically remove it.

> Tag keys for the same resource must not be duplicated.

Tags.N.Value.description_en:
Tag value for user tags.

* Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag value, range: 1–50.
* Separate multiple tag values with &.
* Length range: 0–256 characters. If not specified, defaults to empty.
* Supports input of characters from any language, numbers, spaces ( ), underscores (_), periods (.), colons (:), slashes (/), equals signs (=), plus signs (+), hyphens (-), and @ (@).
* Case sensitive.
* If the tag value starts or ends with a space, the system will automatically remove it.

> If this parameter is provided, `Tags.N.Key` must be specified first.

VpcId.description_en:
VPC ID to be associated with the IPv6 gateway instance.
You can call the [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) API to query the VPC ID.
Each VPC can only be associated with one IPv6 gateway instance. Make sure the VPC to be associated is not already linked to another IPv6 gateway instance.

ClientToken.description_en:
Client token, used to ensure request idempotency

* The client automatically generates a parameter value to ensure uniqueness between requests, preventing repeated operations when the API call times out or there is a server internal error and the client retries multiple times
* Only ASCII characters are supported, and cannot exceed 64 characters
* If ClientToken is not provided, this API call will not perform idempotency validation

Description.description_en:
Network ACL description

* Length must be between 0 and 255 characters
* Must start with a letter, Chinese character, or number. Can include English comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space ( ), equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。)
* If not specified, defaults to an empty string

NetworkAclName.description_en:
Network ACL name

* Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
* Must start with a letter, Chinese character, or number; can include period (.), underscore (_), and hyphen (-)
* If not specified, defaults to the network ACL ID

ProjectName.description_en: Name of the project to which the network ACL belongs. If not specified, it will be added to the default project

Stateful.description_en: Specifies whether it is a stateful ACL.

Tags.N.Key.description_en:

* Use & to separate multiple tag keys
* Cannot start with `volc:` or `sys:`, including any case variation
* Length range is 1–128 characters; supports input of characters in any language, numbers, space ( ), underscore (_), period (.), colon (:), slash (/), equals sign (=), plus sign (+), hyphen (-), and at sign (@)

Tag keys for the same resource cannot be duplicated

Tags.N.Value.description_en:
Tag value for user tags

* Parameter - N: indicates the sequence number of the tag value, range: 1–50
* Use & to separate multiple tag values
* Length range is 0–256 characters; defaults to empty if not specified
* Supports input of characters in any language, numbers, space ( ), underscore (_), period (.), colon (:), slash (/), equals sign (=), plus sign (+), hyphen (-), and at sign (@)

If this parameter is passed, `Tags.N.Key` must be specified first

VpcId.description_en:
ID of the VPC to which the network ACL belongs
You can call the [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) API to query the VPC ID

ClientToken.description_en:
Client Token, used to ensure request idempotency

* The client automatically generates a parameter value to ensure uniqueness across different requests, preventing repeated operations when the client retries due to API timeout or internal server errors
* Only ASCII characters are supported, and the value must not exceed 64 characters

Description.description_en:
Description for the secondary NIC.

* Length limit: 0~255 characters
* Must start with a letter, Chinese character, or number. Can include English comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space ( ), equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。).
* If not specified, defaults to an empty string.

Ipv4Prefix.N.description_en:
Assign a /28 IPv4 address block to the network card
This parameter cannot be specified together with any of the following parameters

* Ipv4PrefixCount
* PrivateIpAddress.N
* SecondaryPrivateIpAddressCount

Ipv4PrefixCount.description_en:
Specify the number of /28 IPv4 subnets to be automatically assigned by the system
This parameter cannot be specified together with any of the following parameters

* Ipv4Prefix.N
* PrivateIpAddress.N
* SecondaryPrivateIpAddressCount

Ipv6Address.N.description_en:
Assign private IPv6 addresses to the network interface card.

* Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the private IPv6 address. The value range depends on the NIC status.
   * When the NIC is in the 'Available' state, the value range is 1~10.
   * When the NIC is in the 'InUse' state, the value range for N is limited by the instance type. For more details, see [Instance Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Introduction-to-instance-types).
* Use & to separate multiple private IPv6 addresses.
* The specified IP must be an available IP in the subnet to which the NIC belongs.

* You cannot specify both `Ipv6Address.N` and `Ipv6AddressCount` at the same time.
* Assigning IPv6 addresses to NICs is currently in beta testing. Only accounts that have completed [Enterprise Certification](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6261/64937) can apply for a trial. To request a trial, please contact your account manager.

Ipv6AddressCount.description_en:
Specify the number of private IPv6 addresses to assign to the NIC.
When this parameter is provided, the system automatically assigns the specified number of available private IPv6 addresses from the subnet to the NIC.
* You cannot specify both `Ipv6Address.N` and `Ipv6AddressCount` at the same time.
* Assigning IPv6 addresses to NICs is currently in beta testing. Only accounts that have completed [Enterprise Certification](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6261/64937) can apply for a trial. To request a trial, please contact your account manager.

Ipv6Prefix.N.description_en:
Assign a /80 IPv6 address block to the network card
This parameter cannot be specified together with any of the following parameters

* Ipv6PrefixCount
* Ipv6AddressCount
* Ipv6Address.N

Ipv6PrefixCount.description_en:
Specify the number of /80 IPv6 subnets to be automatically assigned by the system
This parameter cannot be specified together with any of the following parameters

* Ipv6Prefix.N
* Ipv6AddressCount
* Ipv6Address.N

MacAddress.description_en:
MAC address of the network card. If not specified, the system will assign one by default. If you need to specify, the following constraints apply:

* Format requirements:
   * 48-bit address: Standard 12-digit hexadecimal number
   * Valid characters: Only `0-9`, `A-F`
* Must not conflict within the same region
* Must not conflict with MAC addresses reserved by Volcengine
* Must not conflict with other known communication addresses
* Broadcast address cannot be used: FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF
* Multicast address cannot be used

NetworkInterfaceName.description_en:
Name of the secondary NIC.

* Length limit: 1~128 characters
* Must start with a letter, Chinese character, or number. Can include period (.), underscore (_), and hyphen (-).
* If not specified, defaults to the secondary NIC ID.

PortSecurityEnabled.description_en:
Enable source/destination address check for the network interface card. When enabled, the system automatically blocks traffic where the source or destination address is not the current network interface card.
Please enter the following enumeration values exactly as shown; do not use other values.

* true: Yes
* false (default): No

PrimaryIpAddress.description_en:
Primary private IPv4 address of the auxiliary network interface card

* If specified, it must be an available private IPv4 address in the corresponding subnet.
* If not specified, an available private IPv4 address will be automatically assigned from the corresponding subnet.

PrivateIpAddress.N.description_en:
Specify auxiliary private IPv4 addresses for the network interface card.

* Parameter - N: indicates the sequence number of the auxiliary private IPv4 address; value range: 1–49.
* Use & to separate multiple private IPv4 addresses.
* The specified private IPv4 addresses must be available private IPv4 addresses in the subnet to which the network interface card belongs.

You cannot specify both `SecondaryPrivateIpAddressCount` and `PrivateIpAddress.N` parameters at the same time.

ProjectName.description_en: Name of the project to which the network interface card belongs. If not specified, it will be added to the default project.

SecondaryPrivateIpAddressCount.description_en:
Specify the number of secondary private IPv4 addresses to assign to the secondary NIC, range: 1~49.
When this parameter is provided, the system automatically assigns the specified number of available IPv4 addresses from the subnet as secondary private IPv4 addresses for the newly created NIC.
You cannot specify both `SecondaryPrivateIpAddressCount` and `PrivateIpAddress.N` at the same time.

SecurityGroupIds.N.description_en:
ID of one or more security groups to which the auxiliary network interface card is added.
You can call the [DescribeSecurityGroups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSecurityGroups) API to query the security group ID.

* Security groups must be in the same VPC as the auxiliary network interface card.
* Parameter - N: indicates the sequence number of the security group ID; up to 5 IDs can be specified per call.
* Use & to separate multiple security groups.

ServiceManaged.description_en:
Whether the network card is managed by the service

* true: Yes
* false: No

> This feature is currently in invitation-only testing. To use it, please submit a ticket or contact your account manager.

SubnetId.description_en:
ID of the subnet where the auxiliary network interface card is located.
You can call the [DescribeSubnets](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSubnets) API to query the subnet ID.

Tags.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key for user tags.

* Parameter - N: indicates the sequence number of the tag key; value range: 1–50.
* Use & to separate multiple tag keys.
* Cannot start with `volc:` or `sys:`, in any case.
* Length range is 1–128 characters; supports characters from all languages, numbers, spaces ( ), underscores (_), periods (.), colons (:), slashes (/), equals (=), plus (+), hyphens (-), and at signs (@).
* If the tag key starts or ends with a space, the system will automatically remove it.

Tag keys for the same resource must not be duplicated.

Tags.N.Value.description_en:
Tag value for user tags

* Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag value, range: 1–50
* Use & to separate multiple tag values
* Length range: 0–256 characters; if not specified, defaults to empty
* Supports input of characters from all languages, numbers, spaces ( ), underscores (_), periods (.), colons (:), slashes (/), equals (=), plus (+), hyphens (-), and at (@)
* Case sensitive
* If the tag value starts or ends with a space, the system will automatically remove it

If this parameter is provided, `Tags.N.Key` must be specified first.

TrafficMode.description_en:
Network card communication mode

* HighPerformance: Enables RDMA communication mode
* Standard (default): Uses TCP communication mode

> The feature to enable RDMA communication mode for network cards is currently in invitation-only testing and is only available for accounts that have completed [Enterprise Verification](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6261/64937). To apply for a trial, please contact your account manager.

Type.description_en:
Type of network card. Available values:

* trunk: Trunk network card
* secondary (default): Secondary network card

WithoutSecurityGroup.description_en:
Whether the network card has no security group

* true: Yes
* false: No

> This feature is currently in invitation-only testing. To use it, please submit a ticket or contact your account manager.

ClientToken.description_en:
Client Token, used to ensure request idempotency.

* The client automatically generates a parameter value to ensure that this value is unique across different requests, preventing duplicate operations caused by multiple retries when the API call times out or a server internal error occurs.
* Only ASCII characters are supported, and the length cannot exceed 64 characters.
* If ClientToken is not provided, idempotency verification will not be performed for this API call.

Description.description_en:
Description of the prefix list.

* Length limit is 0–255 characters.
* If not specified, defaults to an empty string.
* Must start with a letter, Chinese character, or number. Can include English commas (,), periods (.), underscores (_), spaces ( ), equals signs (=), hyphens (-), Chinese commas (，), and Chinese periods (。).

DryRun.description_en:
Whether to only pre-check this request.
Please enter the following enumerated values exactly as shown, do not use other values.

* **true**: Sends a check request and does not create the prefix list. Checks include required parameters, request format, and business restrictions. If the check fails, the corresponding error is returned. If the check passes, the error code `DryRunOperation` is returned.
* **false** (default): Sends a normal request. If the check passes, returns HTTP 2xx status code and directly creates the prefix list.

IpVersion.description_en:
IP version type. Values:

* IPv4 (default): IPv4 type.
* IPv6: IPv6 type.

MaxEntries.description_en: Maximum number of entries, that is, the maximum number of entries that can be added to the prefix list. Value range: 1–200.

PrefixListEntries.N.Cidr.description_en:
CIDR of the prefix list entry.

* Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the prefix list entry, range: 1–`MaxEntries`, and N should be in consecutive ascending order.
* Separate multiple CIDRs with &.

PrefixListEntries.N.Description.description_en:
Description of the prefix list entry.

* Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the prefix list entry, range: 1–`MaxEntries`, and N should be in consecutive ascending order.
* Separate multiple descriptions with &.
* Length limit: 0–255 characters.
* If not specified, defaults to an empty string.
* Must start with a letter, Chinese character, or number. Can include English commas (,), periods (.), underscores (_), spaces ( ), equals signs (=), hyphens (-), Chinese commas (，), and Chinese periods (。).

PrefixListName.description_en:
Name of the prefix list.

* Length limit: 1–128 characters.
* Must start with a letter, Chinese character, or number. Can include periods (.), underscores (_), and hyphens (-).
* If not specified, defaults to the prefix list ID.

ProjectName.description_en: Name of the project to which the prefix list belongs. If not specified, it will be added to the default project.

Tags.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key for user tags.

* Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag key, value range: 1–50.
* Separate multiple tag keys with &.
* Cannot start with `volc:` or `sys:`, in any case.
* Length range is 1–128 characters; allows characters from any language, numbers, spaces ( ), underscores (_), periods (.), half-width colons (:), slashes (/), equals signs (=), plus signs (+), hyphens (-), and at signs (@).

Duplicate tag keys are not allowed for the same resource.

If this parameter is provided, `Tags.N.Key` must be specified first.

Description.description_en:
Route entry description.

* Must start with a letter, Chinese character, or number. Can contain English comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space ( ), equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。).
* Length limit: 0–255 characters.
* If not specified, defaults to an empty string.

DestinationCidrBlock.description_en:
Destination CIDR block for the route entry.
* When `NextHopType` is set to "IPv6GW", this parameter can only be set to ::/0.
* Only one of `DestinationCidrBlock` or `DestinationPrefixListId` must be specified.

DestinationPrefixListId.description_en: Prefix list ID. You can call the [DescribePrefixLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribePrefixLists) API to query the prefix list ID. * Only one of `DestinationCidrBlock` or `DestinationPrefixListId` must be specified. * Gateway route tables do not support this parameter.

NextHopId.description_en:
Next hop resource ID.
Enter the correct resource ID based on the next hop type.

NextHopName.description_en: Routing Entry Next Hop Resource Name

NextHopType.description_en: * **Subnet Route Table**: The next hop type for the custom route entry. Valid values: * Instance: ECS instance * HaVip: High-availability virtual IP * NetworkInterface: Secondary ENI * NatGW: NAT gateway * VpnGW: VPN gateway * TransitRouter: Transit router * IPv6GW: IPv6 gateway * CloudConnector: Cloud connector * GWLBEndpoint: Gateway Load Balancer endpoint * **Gateway Route Table**: The next hop type for the custom route entry. Valid values: * NetworkInterface: Secondary ENI * GWLBEndpoint: Gateway Load Balancer endpoint * Gateway Load Balancer, Cloud Connector, IPv6 Gateway, and Gateway Route Table are in invitation-only preview. To try them, contact your account manager. * Custom subnet route tables support GWLBEndpoint. When the destination CIDR block of the GWLBEndpoint and the local route destination CIDR block are the same, the GWLBEndpoint route takes effect. * If the NextHopType parameter of the gateway route table is set to GWLBEndpoint, the value of DestinationCidrBlock can be a subset of the subnet CIDR block, such as /32.

RouteEntryName.description_en:
Routing Entry Name

* Must start with a letter, Chinese character, or number; can include period (.), underscore (_), and hyphen (-)
* Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
* If left blank, defaults to an empty string

RouteTableId.description_en:
Route table ID.
You can call the [DescribeRouteTableList](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeRouteTableList) API to query the route table ID.

AssociateType.description_en:
Type of the route table. The available values are:

* Subnet (default): Subnet route table.
* Gateway: Gateway route table.

ID of the VPC to which the route table belongs.

Description of the security group

Hidden security group, not visible to users

* false: No

ProjectName.description_en: Name of the project to which the security group belongs. If not specified, defaults to the 'default' project

SecurityGroupName.description_en:
Name of the security group

* Length limit: 1–128 characters

Service-managed security group

Type.description_en:
Security group type. Possible values:

* cidr_only: CIDR-Only security group
   * This security group is no longer subject to IP address quota limits and is suitable for scenarios such as automatic resource scaling and large-scale IP address usage
   * Rules for this security group do not support referencing other security groups or prefix lists
* If not specified, defaults to a normal security group

VpcId.description_en:
ID of the VPC to which the security group belongs
You can call the [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) API to query the VPC ID

CidrBlock.description_en:
CIDR block of the subnet.

* The subnet's CIDR block must be within the CIDR block of its VPC.
* The subnet's CIDR block cannot be the same as the destination CIDR block of any route entry in the VPC, but can be a subset of it.
* The subnet mask length depends on the VPC's CIDR block, as follows:
   * 10.XX.XX.XX CIDR block mask range: 8–29
   * 172.16.XX.XX CIDR block mask range: 12–29
   * 192.168.XX.XX CIDR block mask range: 16–29

Description.description_en:
Description of the subnet.

* Length limit: 0–255 characters.
* Must start with a letter, Chinese character, or number. Can include English comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space ( ), equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。).
* Cannot start with `http://` or `https://`.
* If not filled, defaults to an empty string.

Ipv6CidrBlock.description_en:
The last 8 bits of the subnet IPv6 segment (the subnet mask is fixed at /64), value range: 0–255.
* This parameter can only be configured if the VPC specified by `VpcId` has enabled IPv6.
* IPv6 support for VPC is currently in beta testing. Only accounts that have completed [Enterprise Certification](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6261/64937) can apply for a trial. If you need a trial, please contact your account manager.

IsIpv6Only.description_en:
Whether the subnet supports only IPv6 segments.

* true: Yes
* false (default): No

> `CidrBlock` and `IsIpv6Only` cannot be provided at the same time.

SubnetName.description_en:
Name of the subnet.

* Length must be 1–128 characters.
* Must start with a letter, Chinese character, or number. Can include periods (.), underscores (_), and hyphens (-).
* Cannot start with `http://` or `https://`.
* If not specified, the default is the subnet ID.

* The client automatically generates a parameter value to ensure uniqueness between different requests, preventing repeated operations when the API call times out or a server internal error occurs and the client retries multiple times.
* Only ASCII characters are supported, and the value cannot exceed 64 characters.
* If ClientToken is not provided, this API call will not perform idempotency verification.

TagFilters.N.Key.description_en: The tag key of the resource tag. When multiple tag keys are specified, it queries resources that contain all specified tag keys.

TagFilters.N.Values.M.description_en: Tag value for the resource tag. Each tag key can specify up to 3 tag values. If this parameter is not provided, resources associated with all tag values under the specified tag key are queried. If this parameter is set to empty, resources associated with tags under the specified tag key with empty tag values are queried. If multiple tag values are specified for the same tag key, the query returns the set of resources associated with each tag value. If this parameter is provided, TagFilters.N.Key must be specified first.

custom: user tag

> If this parameter is not provided or is empty, all types of tags are queried.

MaxResults.description_en: Number of results per query: default is 10, maximum is 100

NextToken.description_en: Pagination token used to mark the position of pagination. You do not need to set this parameter when calling the API for the first time. For subsequent queries, set the value to the NextToken parameter returned by the previous API call.

ResourceIds.N.description_en:
Resource ID.

* Parameter - N: indicates the sequence number of the resource ID. Maximum 50 per call.
* Separate multiple resource IDs with &.

ResourceType.description_en:
Resource type. Valid values:

* vpc: private network.
* subnet: subnet.
* eni: network interface.
* securitygroup: security group.
* havip: high availability virtual IP.
* routetable: route table.
* networkacl: network ACL.
* flowlog: flow log.
* trafficmirrortarget: traffic mirror target.
* trafficmirrorfilter: traffic mirror filter.
* trafficmirrorsession: traffic mirror session.
* eip: public IP.
* bandwidthpackage: shared bandwidth package.
* ngw: NAT gateway.
* vpngateway: VPN gateway.
* directconnectconnection: physical dedicated connection.
* directconnectgateway: dedicated connection gateway.
* directconnectvirtualinterface: virtual interface.

TagFilters.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key.

* Parameter - N: indicates the sequence number of the tag key, range: 1–10.
* Separate multiple tag keys with &. Multiple tag keys are in an AND relationship, meaning resources with all specified tag keys are queried.
* Duplicates are not allowed.

TagFilters.N.Values.N.description_en:
Tag value.

* The first N: indicates the sequence number of the tag key, range: 1–10.
* The second N: indicates the sequence number of the tag value, range: 1–3. Multiple tag values under the same tag key are in an OR relationship, meaning resources with any of these tag values under the same tag key are queried.
* Separate multiple tag values with &.

* If this parameter is provided, you must first provide TagFilters.N.Key.
* Passing an empty string means querying resources with empty tag values.

TagType.description_en:
Tag type. Valid values:

* custom: user tag.
* system: system tag.

If this parameter is not provided or is empty, all types of tags will be queried.

AddPrefixListEntries.N.Description.description_en:

DryRun.description_en:
Whether to perform a dry run for this request.
Please enter the following enum values exactly as shown, and do not use other values.

* true: Sends a check request without modifying the prefix list. Checks include required parameters, request format, and business restrictions. If the check fails, the corresponding error is returned. If the check passes, the error code `DryRunOperation` is returned.
* false (default): Sends a normal request. If the check passes, returns HTTP 2xx status code and directly modifies the prefix list.

MaxEntries.description_en:
Maximum number of entries, that is, the maximum number of entries that can be added to the prefix list.

* If the prefix list is not associated with any resources, the maximum number of entries is no more than 200.
* If the prefix list is associated with resources, the maximum number of entries is not only limited to 200, but also subject to the quota of the associated resources.

The maximum number of entries in the prefix list will occupy the quota of its associated resources. Modifying the maximum number of entries may cause resources to be unable to associate with the pending prefix list. Please evaluate your business needs carefully before proceeding.

You must specify one of the parameters `CidrIp`, `SourceGroupId`, or `PrefixListId`. If you specify more than one, only one takes effect, with the priority order: `CidrIp` > `SourceGroupId` > `PrefixListId`.

Description.description_en:

* Length limit: 1 ~ 255 characters.
* Leave blank to keep the current configuration.

Policy.description_en:
Access policy. Determines whether the NICs in the security group can access resources corresponding to `CidrIp`, `SourceGroupId`, or `PrefixListId`.

* accept: Allow
* drop: Deny

PortEnd.description_en:
End value of the port range.

* When `Protocol` is tcp or udp, the valid range is 1~65535.
* When `Protocol` is icmp, icmpv6, or all, only -1 is supported, which means no port restriction.

PortStart.description_en:
Start value of the port range.

* When `Protocol` is tcp or udp, the valid range is 1~65535.
* When `Protocol` is icmp, icmpv6, or all, only -1 is supported, which means no port restriction.

PrefixListId.description_en:
ID of the destination address prefix list. All CIDRs in the prefix list are destination addresses.
You can call the [DescribePrefixLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribePrefixLists) API to query the prefix list ID.
* The number of outbound security group rules that can still be added to the current security group must be no less than the maximum number of entries in the prefix list.
* You must provide one of the parameters: `CidrIp`, `SourceGroupId`, or `PrefixListId`. If you provide multiple parameters, only one will take effect, with the priority order being `CidrIp` > `SourceGroupId` > `PrefixListId`.

Priority.description_en:

Value range: 1 ~ 100

Protocol.description_en:

* tcp: TCP protocol
* udp: UDP protocol
* icmp: ICMP protocol
* icmpv6: ICMPV6 protocol

* all: Supports all protocols

SourceGroupId.description_en:

You must specify one of the parameters `CidrIp`, `SourceGroupId`, or `PrefixListId`. If you specify more than one, only one takes effect, with the priority order: `CidrIp` > `SourceGroupId` > `PrefixListId`.

* When `Protocol` is `icmp`, `icmpv6`, or `all`, only `-1` is supported, which means no port restriction.

SourcePortStart.description_en:

* When `Protocol` is `icmp`, `icmpv6`, or `all`, only `-1` is supported, which means no port restriction.

CidrIp.description_en:

You must specify one of the following parameters: `CidrIp`, `SourceGroupId`, or `PrefixListId`. If you specify more than one, only one will take effect, with the following priority: `CidrIp` > `SourceGroupId` > `PrefixListId`.

PortEnd.description_en:
End value of the port range.
